items.title: A profiling harness that measures tick cost, generation cost and frame headroom on the real world
items.summary: Ben ruled (NR-162, 2026-08-13): the partial numbers (33.1 ms/econ tick on the 3x world, 0.45 s generation) are not enough - build a proper profiling harness so hardware requirements and expected lag are measured, not inferred from other instruments.
items.design: RULED 2026-08-13 (NR-162). What exists is incidental: data_creep_harness times ticks as a side effect, step_economy_phase_ms breaks down one phase family. What is owed is a dedicated tools/verify harness that reports, on the real generated 3x world: generation wall time by stage, econ tick cost by phase over a long run (warm-up vs settled), and the derived per-day/per-quarter latency a player feels at each game speed. Output a table diffable across commits so perf regressions are visible the way data creep is. Frame-side (render) cost stays out of scope for a headless harness - note the boundary; the live-app frame cost is a separate measurement. Push to the verifier-headless skill on landing.

items.title: The inter-body demand pull nets against a supply that is always zero, so outposts are pulled by gross home demand
items.summary: inject_interbody_demand subtracts home supply from home demand, intending the home body's UNMET demand. But clear_markets zeroes every market's supply immediately before the injection and the supply writes land after it, so home supply is identically zero at the read. The subtraction is a no-op: every outpost market receives pull_fraction of the home body's GROSS demand every tick, distance-discounted.
items.design:
FOUND 2026-08-13 by the verifier-review pass over the BL-382 slice, which had proposed to
document this gate as dormant. It is not dormant - it is live, and it measures the wrong thing.

## The sequence

In clear_markets (market_clearing.cpp):

1. mc.supply.fill(0.0f) / mc.demand.fill(0.0f) for every market
2. inject_population_demand
3. inject_background_demand
4. inject_interbody_demand   <- reads home supply HERE, and it is 0
5. ... the auto-surplus and order-book paths write supply

So the shortfall expression (home demand minus home supply) equals home demand exactly. The
gate that skips a resource when the shortfall is non-positive therefore opens for every
resource carrying any demand at all.

## Why it matters

maybe_spawn_market spawns an outpost market on any off-home building completion. From that
tick the outpost receives pull_fraction of the home body's GROSS demand for every resource,
divided by the distance falloff - injected as demand, which price resolution reads. Outpost
prices are set by a number that was meant to be a shortfall and is actually a gross total.
This is a live input to every outpost price, not a dormant branch.

## The fix is a sequencing question, not an arithmetic one

Netting honestly means reading a home supply this pass has not computed yet. Options, to
settle at promotion:

a) Move the injection after the supply writes. Truest to the intent, but those writes are
   themselves demand-sensitive (auto-surplus yields to standing orders), so this risks a
   two-pass dependency in a pass whose ordering is already load-bearing.
b) Net against the PREVIOUS tick's supply, captured before the fill. One tick of lag,
   trivially deterministic, honest about what it is.
c) Drop the subtraction and state plainly that the pull is on gross demand, re-tuning
   pull_fraction to compensate. Simplest, and arguably what the mechanism has always done.

RECOMMENDATION: (b). It preserves the design's stated intent, costs one stored array, and
reorders nothing. Whatever is chosen, the code comment and MARKETS.md must stop describing a
netting that does not happen - both were corrected on 2026-08-13 to describe the real
behaviour and point here.

## MEASURED 2026-08-13 — and the recommendation above is REFUTED

`tools/verify/interbody_pull_harness.cpp` was written to settle this item against the real
Lua-authored economy rather than a hand-built fixture. Two things came out of it, and the
second one blocks this item.

**1. R1 confirmed, structurally.** At the injector's read point the subtraction is a no-op:
the gate opens for every resource carrying any demand, on every build tested. The item's
core claim stands.

**2. Option (b) is not implementable as written, because 'home supply' is not the home
body's supply.** The pull reads ONE of the home body's many markets (the lowest-id pick from
an unordered container). On the canonical MSVC build that market holds 1491.4 supply of the
body's 7497.9 and 4.0 demand of its 33.9; on a g++ build of the same seed it holds 0.0
supply of 2863.3. So 'net against the previous tick's supply' silences 33% of the pull on
one toolchain and 0% on the other. The netting cannot be corrected before the thing being
netted against is well-defined.

That defect is filed as **BL-406 (the home market is an arbitrary pick)**, and this item now
requires it. Settle BL-406 first; this item's a/b/c choice should then be made in the same
pass, because aggregating over the body changes what a corrected netting would do.

**A note on the earlier reasoning.** This item's own text cited BL-381's finding that home
supply exceeds home demand by two to three orders of magnitude. That is right at BODY level
(7497.9 vs 33.9) and does not describe the market the gate reads. A claim can be true of the
economy and false of the code path that matters - which is the whole reason this was measured
rather than argued.

## RULING 2026-08-15 (Ben, elicitation form): defer, decide after BL-406 lands

Ben took BL-406 option (c) — a per-counterpart-market pull — and explicitly deferred this
item's own a/b/c to after that lands. Correct sequencing: (c) changes WHAT is being netted
against (a specific counterpart market's supply, not a body aggregate or an arbitrary pick),
so choosing a netting rule now would be choosing it against a model that is about to be
replaced. Outpost prices are cleared to move, so option (c) here — drop the subtraction and
re-tune — is no longer ruled out on magnitude grounds.

Stays blocked on BL-406. Re-open the a/b/c choice in the same pass that lands it.

## LANDED 2026-08-17, in the same commit as BL-406

Option (b) taken, as originally recommended - and it only became implementable once BL-406 gave
the netting a well-defined thing to net against. `clear_markets` captures every market's supply
via `snapshot_market_supply` immediately BEFORE its reset loop, and the injector subtracts the
COUNTERPART market's snapshot supply. One tick of lag, no reordering of a pass whose ordering is
load-bearing, no new persisted state, save format untouched.

(a) stayed rejected for the reason first given: the supply writes are demand-sensitive, so moving
the injection below them makes this a two-pass dependency. (c) - drop the subtraction and re-tune
- was live again once outpost prices were cleared to move, but there was no longer any reason to
take it: the shortfall now means something.

Measured on seed 0: the netting bites on exactly one of three pulled resources, whose counterpart
holds 260.7 supply against 5.5 demand and correctly pulls nothing. The other two net against a
counterpart supply of genuinely 0.0 and pull their full demand. So the netting is neither a no-op
nor the pull-killer the pre-change harness warned a naive correction would be.

Guard: `interbody_pull_harness` C3 (two assertions - the silencing, and the surviving pull's
exact arithmetic), both observed to FAIL against the pre-change build.

Authority moved to docs/economy/MARKETS.md § Spontaneous market emergence.

items.title: Hiring costs credits since BL-394, and no UI surface shows the price
items.summary: BL-394 gave hire_unit a real credit cost. The hire control in the Selection panel shows a unit name and a Hire button - no cost, no affordability greying - while its sibling road-tier controls each show cost and validity, and the Build door shows a credit total and disables when unaffordable. The AI player now reads the price from ACTIONS.json; the human is told only after the fact, by a generic refusal string.
items.design:
FILED 2026-08-13 from the verifier-review pass on the BL-394 slice.

The asymmetry is the point: the word interface (ACTIONS.json) documents the cost formula for
the AI player, and the human-facing surface does not show it at all. A player who cannot
afford a unit clicks Hire and gets a generic refusal that says neither which leg failed nor
how much was needed.

What to add, matching the sibling controls already in the same panel:

- the credit cost on the row, read from the registry (hire_base_cost plus hire_cost_per_power
  times the roster row's power_mod) - never re-derived in the UI
- greyed/disabled when the corp cannot afford it, in the Build door's idiom
- the resource half of the cost too, where the row is gated on stockpile

Rule 0b applies if any sizing is ambiguous: report the current row measurements before
changing layout. Update the QUESTION_LOG entry for the hire control. ACTIONS.json should not
need changing - this is display only, the press semantics are unchanged.

items.title: The inter-body pull reads one arbitrary market as 'the home body', and which one is not stable across toolchains
items.summary: inject_interbody_demand takes market_for_body(home_body) - the lowest-id market of the 17 the home body carries - and treats its demand and supply as the whole body's. Measured: that market holds 12% of the body's demand and a variable share of its supply. Because w.markets is unordered, the pick differs across standard libraries, so the pull's magnitude (and BL-404's answer) depends on an implementation accident rather than on the economy.
items.design:
FOUND 2026-08-13 by interbody_pull_harness, written to settle BL-404 and which turned up
the larger defect underneath it.

## What the pull thinks 'home' means

`inject_interbody_demand` opens with:

    const entity_id home_market_id = market_for_body(w, w.home_body);
    const market_component& home = w.markets.at(home_market_id);

and then treats `home.demand` / `home.supply` as THE HOME BODY'S demand and supply. But
`market_for_body` returns the LOWEST-ID market on the body, and BL-096 carves many markets
onto the home body. Measured on the canonical MSVC build, seed 0, 60 ticks:

  * home body markets            : 17
  * body totals                  : supply 7497.9, demand 33.9
  * the market the pull READS    : supply 1491.4, demand 4.0  (12% of body demand)

So every outpost market in the game is price-supported in proportion to roughly an eighth of
the home body's appetite, chosen by an arbitrary id ordering.

## The instability is the sharpest part

The same harness on a g++/WSL build of the same seed reports 8 markets, body supply 2863.3,
and a read market carrying 0.0 supply. Same seed, same source, different standard library:
`w.markets` is an unordered container, so the lowest id is not a stable choice of market
across toolchains. Same-seed reproducibility WITHIN a binary (the determinism invariant) is
untouched and still holds - this is not a determinism violation. But it does mean the
identity of 'the home market' is an implementation accident, and a price input should not be.

It also decides BL-404's answer: on one build a corrected netting silences 33% of the pull,
on the other 0%. That is why BL-404 cannot be settled until this is.

## Options

a) **Aggregate over the body.** Sum demand (and supply) across every market on the home body.
   Truest to what the code says it means. Multiplies the pull roughly 8x on today's numbers,
   so pull_fraction wants re-tuning in the same change, and outpost prices will move.
b) **Name the home market explicitly.** Give the world a `primary_market` per body, chosen at
   generation and stored, so the pick is authored rather than incidental. Cheaper, stable,
   and keeps the current magnitude - but leaves 'the home body's demand' meaning one
   market's demand, which is what the code claims it is not.
c) **Pull per-market rather than per-body.** Each outpost market reads the home market that
   is its actual counterpart. Most faithful to a trade model; the largest change, and it
   needs a notion of counterpart markets that does not exist yet.

RECOMMENDATION: (a), together with re-tuning pull_fraction against the measured curve, and
with BL-404's netting decided in the same pass since the two interact. (b) is the cheap
stopgap if outpost prices must not move yet.

## Guard

`interbody_pull_harness` (tools/verify) asserts the structural half - several markets exist,
the pull reads one, its demand is a fraction of the body's - and PRINTS the varying half
rather than asserting it, so it stays green on either toolchain while keeping the numbers in
front of whoever fixes this.

## RULING 2026-08-15 (Ben, elicitation form): option (c), per-counterpart-market pull

Option (c) is taken over the recommended (a). The pull becomes per-market: each outpost
market reads the home market that is its actual counterpart, rather than any body-level
aggregate. The 'home body's demand' framing is retired entirely - the defect this item
names is dissolved rather than repaired, because no single market is asked to stand for a
body any more.

**Outpost prices are cleared to move** (same ruling), so magnitude preservation is not a
constraint on the design. `pull_fraction` is re-tuned against whatever curve (c) produces.

Consequence: the missing piece is now the load-bearing one - a notion of COUNTERPART
MARKETS does not exist in the model. That is the first task at promotion, ahead of touching
`inject_interbody_demand` at all: define what makes a home market the counterpart of an
outpost market (resource overlap, ownership, proximity, or an explicit link recorded at
`maybe_spawn_market` time), and settle whether the relation is one-to-one or many-to-many.
Difficulty raised 3 -> 4 to reflect it.

`interbody_pull_harness` should gain the per-counterpart assertion as the new structural
guard once the relation is defined; its current 'the pull reads one market of many' assertion
becomes obsolete by construction.

## LANDED 2026-08-17, with BL-404 in the same commit

The counterpart relation, as defined at promotion: per RESOURCE, the home-body market carrying
the greatest demand for that resource, lowest market id breaking ties. Many-to-one keyed on the
resource, not one-to-one - the outpost dimension collapses because every home-body market sits
at the same distance from a given outpost, so the falloff already carries it. Per-(outpost,
resource) counterparts would only mean something once markets have a per-market haul cost.

Order-independent by construction (strictly-greater demand, then smaller id), which is what
closes the cross-toolchain instability that was the sharpest half of this item.

Measured on seed 0: the home body carries 9 markets; two of three pulled resources on the test
outpost now pull at 2.8x their old size, and one is silenced by BL-404's netting. Outpost prices
moved, as the ruling cleared them to. `pull_fraction` was NOT re-tuned - NR-277 records why and
folds it into BL-440.

Guard: `interbody_pull_harness` section C, asserted BEHAVIOURALLY against the injector's output
so it could be compiled and run against the pre-change build - where all three of its assertions
FAILED. The old 'the pull reads one market of many' assertion was reworded rather than deleted;
it is now the record of the defect, not a claim about the shipped path.

Authority moved to docs/economy/MARKETS.md § Spontaneous market emergence.

items.title: AI decision feed - a ledger window over the decision ring and the history log's decision/agency topics
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-14 from the spectator-mode design session. Every strategic decision the scorer takes ALREADY records its own rationale - corp_decision carries the winning score, the runner-up score and a reason code (corp_command.hpp), pushed to world::ai_decisions (256-entry ring) AND permanently to world::history_log under the `decision` and `agency` topics. Nothing in src/ui/ reads either store: a grep for corp_decision / decision_ring / agency_event across src/ui + src/core hits only session_history.cpp. The reasoning is in memory, forever, unread. This is the cheapest and highest-value piece of spectator mode - the data exists, only the window is missing.

items.title: Spectator god view - lift the survey mask, the activity fog and the rival-internals redaction, in the UI layer only
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-14. A spectator currently sees LESS than the AI it is watching. The planetary canvas is survey-masked (survey_tile_visible, body_surface_canvas.cpp), the comms feed is deliberately redacted to one nation-level aggregate event per tick (session_history.cpp, honouring the BL-068 competitor-visibility rule), and selecting a rival corp yields name / nation / starting capital / asset count and nothing else (entity_summary.cpp draw_corporation_summary). Spectator mode needs a god view that lifts all three - and needs to lift them WITHOUT touching world/* or the blackboard export, because those are what keep the AI honest. [LANDED 2026-08-19 @ merge 57e596f, awaiting R1's live click-through (needs a spectate entry path — the toggle is spectate-only by construction). 7 captures eyeballed; off-path byte-identity by construction + determinism harnesses green. Comms-redaction lift deliberately deferred (post-time store, needs read-time-filter design — DISCOVERY.md carries the note).]
items.design:
## The rule this breaks, and why that is legitimate

DISCOVERY.md's competitor-visibility rule (BL-068) and the two fogs exist to make the
player earn information. **In spectator mode there is no player** (BL-409), so there is
nobody being cheated. The rule protects a competitive relationship that spectating does
not instantiate.

That argument only holds if the lift is **strictly presentational**. The hard line:

- **May change:** what `src/ui/*` draws and what the comms feed prints.
- **May NOT change:** `world/*` state, `survey_tile_visible`, the activity-fog store, or
  `export_corp_blackboard`. The blackboard's whole value is that it is visibility-honest
  (corp_ai.hpp: rival buildings existence/type/tile ONLY, never cash, pools, recipes or
  workforce). A god view that reached into the export would silently give a future agent
  player telepathy, and STRATEGIES.md § Resolutions already settled that question - Ben,
  2026-08-06: *"No additional information for the AI."*

So the flag is read at the draw call, never at the source. Enforce it by construction:
the spectator flag lives in `ui_state`, and `world/*` never sees it.

## The three lifts

1. **Survey mask.** `body_surface_canvas.cpp` gates per-tile detail on
   `survey_tile_visible(body.survey, ...)`. Under spectate, treat every region as
   revealed. The `UNSURVEYED` / `Surveying n/m` header suffix stays - it is now
   *information about the AI's own blindness*, which is exactly what a spectator wants to
   read, and it becomes far more interesting once you can see what it is missing.
2. **Comms redaction.** `post_nation_agency_comms` posts one nation-voiced line per nation
   per tick, the heaviest event only, by design. Under spectate, post per-corp and
   unthrottled. Keep the nation voice as an option rather than deleting it - the redacted
   feed is the one a player will ship with, so it must stay exercised.
3. **Rival internals.** `draw_corporation_summary` gains the full readout under spectate:
   cash, per-body pools, running recipes, workforce targets, reserve floor, and the
   should-have buffer. All of it is already computable from public functions
   (`corp_reserve_floor`, `corp_should_have_buffer`, `estimate_building_profit`).

## The tell to design for

When the mask is lifted, a spectator should still be able to see **where the AI's own
fog is**. A build the scorer never considered because the tile was unsurveyed is one of
the most legible strategy signals in the game, and it is invisible if god view simply
erases the distinction. Render revealed-but-unsurveyed tiles with a marker rather than
as ordinary revealed ground.

## Obligations

DISCOVERY.md gains a section on the spectator exemption when this lands (not before -
the authority doc time-slices). `question_log.json` entries for the changed surfaces.

items.title: Spectator mode has no human seat - every corp is scored, and player_entity becomes a viewpoint rather than an ownership claim
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-14. The scorer explicitly skips the player's corp - corp_ai.cpp:465 and :499, and corp_strategic_eval_due is documented "Always false for the player corp". Spectating therefore shows a race with one runner standing still, and one specialist corp's worth of demand missing from the economy. Ben's ruling, 2026-08-14, reframed the fix: in spectator mode there is no need to mark a corp as played by a human at all - "'who plays your corp' collapses as a question". The mode does not hand the player's corp to the AI; it asserts that no corp is a player's.

items.title: Attention director - follow the tick's heaviest decision, and jump to any decision from the feed
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-14. Nothing moves the camera on its own, so a spectator stares at one body while the interesting build happens two bodies away. Two affordances: click a decision-feed row to select its subject and navigate the zoom ladder to it, and an opt-in auto-follow that each econ tick moves to that tick's heaviest decision. The severity ordering already exists - session_history.cpp's severity_of ranks idled/demolished (4) above built/hired (3) above recipe_switch/resumed (2) above road/workforce/survey/order traffic (1).
items.design:
## Two modes, one mechanism

**Jump-to (manual).** A decision-feed row knows its `corp_decision.command`, which
carries the target entity. Clicking it sets `selected_entity` and drives the zoom
ladder to the owning body - the same descend-by-click path CANVASES.md already
defines, invoked programmatically rather than by a press.

**Auto-follow (opt-in, off by default).** Each econ tick, pick the heaviest decision
by the existing `severity_of` ordering, break ties by lowest corp id (determinism),
and navigate there. Reuse `severity_of` rather than authoring a second ranking - a
second ordering that disagrees with the comms feed's would be a bug generator.

## The pacing problem, which is the real design work

At speed 5 an econ tick resolves every ~11 real seconds (16x multiplier, 2 s/day at
1x, 90-day quarter). Auto-follow that snaps the camera every 11 seconds is unwatchable,
and at lower speeds it is dead air. Three things make it read:

1. **Ease, never snap.** Route through `interp.cpp`, over roughly a second. The
   transition is what tells the eye *where it went*, which is most of the value.
2. **Hold a minimum dwell.** Never retarget within ~4 real seconds of the last move,
   even if a heavier decision lands. A camera that twitches shows nothing.
3. **Ignore the noise floor.** Do not follow severity-1 traffic (roads, workforce
   nudges, order-book churn) at all. Follow builds, demolitions, idles and hires -
   the decisions that change the industrial landscape.

## Determinism

The director is presentation and must not touch the sim. Camera state lives in
`ui_state`; nothing in `world/*` learns that it exists.

## Obligations

CANVASES.md gains the programmatic-navigation note when this lands. `question_log.json`
for the follow toggle; `ACTIONS.json` for the new controls.

> ⟳ 2026-08-19: FIRST TASK (verdict O4): the spectate initial viewpoint fix folds in here — spectate currently inherits the would-be player corp, which on seed 0 is insolvent and asset-less (NR-231). Opening camera = heaviest-decision corp of the first evaluated tick, a natural special case of auto-follow.

items.title: Emergent-strategy readout - per-corp run summary of verb mix, spend by priority bucket, and reason-code tally
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-14. The literal answer to the question that prompted the spectator session - Ben, 2026-08-14: watch AI play "and discover what strategies emerge from the current game", to have "a better way to describe and explain our main aims". The decision feed (BL-407) shows the moves; this shows the SHAPE across a run. Aggregates the same two stores into a per-corp profile: verb mix, spend split across the must-have / should-have / nice-to-have buckets (corp_ai.hpp bucket_for_reason), reason-code tally, and how those shift over the run. [LANDED 2026-08-19 @ merge d3d9e6e, awaiting R1's live click (nav slot 12). Recorder-pattern aggregation (O(new decisions)/tick), 64-quarter window, counts-not-credits, score fields excluded per the NR-226 fence; 3 captures eyeballed; question_log pair drafted.]
items.design:
## What a strategy looks like in this engine

The scorer has no strategy object - `corp_strategy` is a direct read of
`industrial_focus`, kept as its own name precisely so it can diverge later
(corp_ai.hpp). So an emergent strategy is not a thing to read out of a field; it is a
**distribution over decisions**. Three distributions carry almost all of it:

1. **Verb mix.** What fraction of this corp's decisions were builds, dials, surveys,
   roads, hires, orders. An expander and a consolidator have visibly different mixes.
2. **Spend by priority bucket.** `bucket_for_reason` already classifies every reason
   into must-have (solvency defence) / should-have (feed the running assets) /
   nice-to-have (expansion). A corp spending most of its run in must-have is drowning;
   one that stays in nice-to-have is running unopposed. This is the single most
   legible health signal available, and it is free - the mapping is a pure function
   that already exists.
3. **Reason-code tally.** Which reasons actually fired. § 10h's idle/resume
   oscillation would have shown here as two reciprocal codes dominating the tally.

## Over the run, not just at the end

Each quarter, plot the bucket split as a stacked band per corp. The interesting
artifact is the *transition* - the quarter a corp falls out of nice-to-have and never
recovers is the quarter it lost, and being able to point at that quarter is exactly
the "describe and explain our main aims" the session asked for. Use `charts.cpp` and
the existing per-tick history recorder pattern in `session_history.cpp` rather than a
new store.

## Feeds two things beyond spectating

- **STRATEGIES.md's invention loop.** The deck is AI-invented and the schema authored
  (Ben, 2026-08-06), and a card earns its slot by same-seed comparison. This readout is
  the measuring instrument that comparison needs; without it "the card worked" is an
  assertion.
- **BL-279 (trace corpus).** The same aggregation labels a run, which is what a
  fine-tuning corpus needs alongside the traces.

## Honesty constraint

Report the distribution; do not name the strategy. A label like "aggressive expander"
rendered from three thresholds is a fiction the reader will trust more than it earns,
and naming it would also pre-empt STRATEGIES.md's settled position that the deck is
discovered rather than authored. Show the mix and let the shape speak.

> ⟳ 2026-08-19: FENCE (NR-226 / verdict O1): decision-ring score fields are EXCLUDED from aggregation — runner_up can legitimately exceed winning_score because candidate_before sorts by priority bucket before score (AI_OPPONENT.md § 10i). If margins are ever wanted, normalise within priority bucket first. The readout aggregates verb mix, spend buckets and reason codes only, as designed.

items.title: Live agent control seam - let an external agent play a rendered session, not just a headless one
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-14. --serve (BL-278) is headless-only: main.cpp branches to the line-protocol server INSTEAD of app::run, so an agent playing through the MCP seam is invisible while it plays. Spectating the deterministic scorer (BL-407 to BL-411) and spectating a language model are therefore different jobs, and this is the second one. Deliberately filed as its own item so the first five do not silently acquire its cost. [LANDED 2026-08-19 @ merge e88636b, awaiting R3's canvas-eyeball half (Ben; app left open with --host-agent). Everything else green: 22/22 harness incl. transcript-replay determinism over a real socket; R4 listen-only confirmed by verifier-review; the actor gate ALSO proven live when the first watch session read as the wrong corp and was refused. First watch session ran this date: qwen2.5:3b-instruct attached, ticks released 1..8 through the gated clock.]
items.design:
## The structural gap

`main.cpp` dispatches on argv: `--serve` runs the line-protocol loop, `--verify` runs
the headless capture harness, `--autostart` runs the GUI. They are exclusive branches.
The seam an agent drives and the loop that draws pixels never coexist, so the only way
to observe an agent's play today is to read a transcript after the fact.

## Shape

The honest version is: `app::run`'s frame loop gains a non-blocking drain of pending
protocol requests, serviced at a tick boundary rather than mid-frame. Requests apply
through `apply_corp_command` - the same seam the presses and the scorer already use, so
no third code path appears. `ADVANCE_TICK` under a live session means *release the clock
for one econ tick*, which is a different contract from the headless one and is the part
that needs designing rather than coding.

## The three real problems

1. **Clock ownership.** Headless, the agent drives the clock. Live, the wall clock does.
   Either the agent gates the clock (and the session stalls whenever the model is
   thinking - honest, and probably right for watching) or the clock free-runs (and the
   agent plays a moving target). Pick deliberately; do not let it fall out of the
   implementation.
2. **Determinism.** A wall-clock-paced session where commands land on whichever tick
   they happen to arrive is **not replayable**, which forfeits the property AI_OPPONENT.md
   § 10h leans on hardest (*"a play transcript is a replay artifact"*). Applying commands
   only at tick boundaries, in arrival order, recorded, preserves it. This is the reason
   to gate the clock.
3. **Transport.** stdio is taken by the app's own console. Needs a socket, and the
   engine still ships no HTTP client, no API key, no cloud dependency - the hard
   invariant of AI_OPPONENT.md § 10. A local socket the agent connects TO is inside
   that line; anything the engine dials out to is not.

## Relation to the rest

Composes with BL-407 (the feed shows the agent's moves alongside the scorer's) and
BL-408 (god view). It does NOT need BL-409 - an agent playing a corp is the opposite
of the no-seat mode; the seat is occupied, just not by a human. Both configurations
should be reachable.

## Research use, not the shipped rival

The § 10g ruling stands: the deterministic scorer remains the action generator for the
shipped rival. This is the research and diagnostics seam § 10h argues already pays.

items.title: Under spectate, disable the player's press affordances rather than leave them live with no seat behind them
items.summary: Split from BL-409 R4 (2026-08-14 housekeeping) - UI work outside the files the implementing agent owned. Construction placement, order entry and workforce dials still respond under spectate even though no corp is the player's to command. Not hidden, DISABLED and legible, so the mode reads as a window rather than a broken game (BL-409's own design already states this bar).
items.design:
Gate the existing press handlers on `ui_state::spectating`, greyed rather than removed, per the disabled-not-hidden rule BL-409 already set. Small: no new affordance, just a guard on ones that exist.

> ⟳ 2026-08-19 (review #8, integration): the seam x spectate collision joins this item's scope — app.cpp sets the seam actor to player_entity every frame, and under spectate that corp is ALSO scorer-driven, so --host-agent in a spectated session double-drives one seat. Until the interaction is designed, the rule is: REFUSE seam attach while spectating (or refuse spectate while a client is attached), whichever press comes second. Same spirit as this item's R4: under spectate, presses that would act on a corp are withdrawn - the agent seam is such a press.

items.title: resource_type name lookup is hand-implemented three times with no check that they agree, and it has already caused one startup crash
items.summary: Filed from NR-175 (2026-08-14 housekeeping). Root cause of the 2026-08-12 startup crash (`fatal error: Unknown resource 'medical_supplies' in world_gen.kepler_market.base_price`): resource_type name lookup exists as three independent hand-maintained tables in three anonymous namespaces, and no two agree against the 42-value enum. The crash was patched around; the desync generator itself is unfixed.
items.design:
Consolidate to one canonical name table (RESOURCES.md already owns the canonical list) with the other two call sites reading through it, plus a loud failure (not a silent fallback) on lookup miss so a future gap fails at the point it is introduced rather than three tables later, unpredictably, at runtime.

LANDED 2026-08-19 (Batch Delivery). Consolidated recipe_registry.cpp and world_gen_config.cpp's independent resource_from_name tables into one shared src/world/resource_names.{hpp,cpp}. Both old tables were already complete (all 38 resource_type values covered), so this is a pure structural fix with zero behavior change today - it closes the DESYNC RISK the item was filed over, not a live desync. presentation.cpp's separate enum->display-name table (src/ui, a different concern - UI display strings, not a Lua-name parser) was left as-is per layering (world/ must not depend on ui/); it has three still-unauthored rows (charcoal, iron_blooms, trade_goods_misc) noted as a content gap, not fixed here - see NR-374.

items.title: Plain `ctest` still runs the harnesses labelled `sweep` and documented as excluded from the routine gate - a label excludes nothing on its own
items.summary: Filed from NR-194 (2026-08-14 housekeeping). history_sim_harness, history_sweep and data_creep_harness carry a `sweep` CTest label and are documented as excluded from the routine gate, but the gate invocation that actually excludes them (`ctest -LE sweep`) is nowhere enforced - a bare `ctest` runs them anyway. This session two orphaned history_sim_harness processes were found burning ~5,200 CPU-seconds each from a killed run, starving the machine.

items.title: ai_skill_harness's golden bands drift with every AI-adjacent landing and nobody owns re-blessing them - 13 assertions have been red for at least two sessions
items.summary: Merges NR-169 and NR-220 (2026-08-14 housekeeping) - the same harness, the same unowned stewardship gap, raised twice a day apart. NR-169: BL-366 and BL-130 both moved the bands they touch (5→8, 8→9) without a re-run. NR-220: the harness was independently confirmed 13-red both before and after an unrelated batch, so the red is stale, not a regression - but nothing currently distinguishes "stale red" from "new failure" at a glance.

items.title: The build candidate score is quadratic in net margin - `net / payback` collapses to net squared over capex, and the tuning was calibrated against that curve without anyone deciding it should be there
items.summary: Filed from NR-230 (2026-08-14 housekeeping), found by running the new AI decision feed against real data. corp_ai.cpp computes `payback = capex / net` then scores `net / payback`, which is algebraically `net^2 / capex` - reads as capital efficiency, behaves as a margin bias (doubling margin quadruples the score; doubling cost only halves it). Real 144-tick runs score in the ~1.2 billion range. focus_weight/jitter/glut were tuned against this curve, so changing it silently retunes every rival's build behaviour and every blessed golden.
items.design:
Two steps, deliberately not one commit. (1) Rewrite the expression to say what it does - `c.score = (net * net / capex) * ...` - a no-op refactor, zero behavioural change, that stops the code lying to the next reader. (2) Separately and deliberately, decide whether the quadratic bias is wanted: keep it and comment why, or replace it with an explicit linear metric and re-tune the multipliers against the new curve (accepting the golden reshuffle that follows). Do not do (2) as a drive-by inside (1).

> ⟳ 2026-08-19 (N1 audit): HELD, not open. Step 1 landed+verified at 56bcb86 (score = net²/capex, corp_ai.cpp:694-713); req group quadratic-build-score-honest R1–R4 complete, R5 pending. Step 2 is Ben's call (NR-265 re-scope, NR-268) and should sequence AFTER BL-439's golden re-bless. Consider splitting step 2 to its own item at next triage.
items.step_1_landed:
Landed 2026-08-17, Sprint 19 — THE HONEST REWRITE ONLY. corp_ai.cpp's extraction build candidate now scores `(net * net / capex) * focus_weight * jitter * glut` directly; the intermediate `payback = capex / net` is gone. A comment states the quadratic bias, why it is retained (focus_weight/jitter/glut were tuned against this curve, and every blessed golden records a world evolved under it), and that replacing it is step 2.

THE "ZERO BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE" CLAIM IN THIS ITEM'S DESIGN WAS NOT ESTABLISHED WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN. `net / (capex / net)` and `(net * net) / capex` round differently in float, so the rewrite could have moved every candidate score, hence world evolution, hence every blessed golden — which would have made step 1 exactly the thing the item says it is not. Measured rather than assumed, A/B on the pinned MSVC 14.44 build against this branch's base: ai_skill_harness byte-identical across all 5 seeds (ALL PASS, 0 failures, both sides); spectator_determinism byte-identical, played=855E07DE529684EC / spectated=5AC90B4ACE717FCF unchanged. It IS free on this toolchain — by rounding luck, not by algebra. Had it moved, the golden re-bless would have been part of step 1 and reported as such rather than smuggled in. Recorded as NR-268. Full local CTest logic tier green — the gate the remote session could not run at all.

Corrected in passing: the military_base candidate's comment claimed it must never out-bid "a genuine extraction/processing net-positive candidate". There is no processing_facility build candidate in this scorer at all — see BL-439.

Requirements group: quadratic-build-score-honest (R1-R4 complete, R5 = step 2, pending).
items.step_2_open:
STILL OWED, AND BEN'S CALL: decide whether the quadratic bias is wanted — keep it with the reasoning recorded, or replace it with an explicit linear metric and re-tune the multipliers against the new curve, accepting the golden reshuffle.

RE-SCOPED BEFORE IT IS TAKEN (NR-265, 2026-08-17). This item was filed on the premise, inherited from BL-436, that the curve is why the AI prefers mines to processors. It is not. corp_ai.cpp emits corp_verb::build from exactly two sites — the ranked_sites loop hard-coded to extraction_site, and one military_base candidate. A processing_facility is never a candidate, so no curve over this candidate set can prefer one. "The AI prefers mines" is STRUCTURAL, and BL-439 is the item that addresses it. What step 2 actually decides is narrower than it looks: how extraction sites are ranked against each other and against the flat-scored military base. Landing BL-439 first would change what step 2 is choosing between, so the sequence is worth deciding before the curve is.

items.title: Spectator mode inherits whichever corp the player would have been as its opening viewpoint, and on the default seed that corp is insolvent with no assets
items.summary: Filed from NR-231 (2026-08-14 housekeeping), found building BL-409's determinism harness. The generated player corp on seed 0 ends 300 ticks at roughly -80,500 credits with zero extractors and zero processors - not a player-specific generation bug (two rivals share the state), but it means a spectated campaign on the default seed opens the camera on a corp doing nothing, which undercuts the whole point of watching strategies emerge (BL-407/BL-411).
items.design: Spectator mode should choose its opening viewpoint deliberately - the best-endowed corp by a stable property (not by outcome, which would be circular), the same selection rule BL-409's own harness uses for its controlled A/B. Small: one function, called once when spectate mode starts, or folded into BL-410's attention-director work if that lands first.

items.title: The AI decision feed rebuilds every row from scratch every frame while open, with no clipper - and spectator mode is exactly the mode that keeps it open at 16x
items.summary: Filed from NR-233 S1 (2026-08-14 housekeeping, cold review of the BL-407 diff). assemble_rows reverse-walks the history log and rebuilds up to 512 feed_rows (2-3 std::strings, 1-3 map lookups each) EVERY FRAME the feed is open, then renders ~6 ImGui items per row (~3000/frame) with TextWrapped doing word-wrap layout. No ImGuiListClipper. This project has a frame-budget HUD (BL-249) and has already paid down one O(corps x tiles) per-tick cost (BL-253); this is the same shape, on the render side, in the one surface designed to stay open while the sim runs fast.
items.design: Cache the assembled row vector and rebuild only when the underlying tick advances (the ring/log can only grow between renders, not change retroactively), not on every ImGui frame. Do before spectator mode (BL-408) is used at speed for any length of time - that is precisely the condition that makes this cost real.

items.title: A held sell order still credits market inventory at listing time
items.summary: Found by the seam-batch review barrier (2026-08-14): market_clearing.cpp credits a standing order's LISTED quantity to mc.inventory (~line 578, the BL-130 real-inventory seam) before clearing runs. Pre-BL-386 everything listed also sold, so listing == selling; under the reservation rule a held order (floor above the resolved price) sells nothing, yet the market's inventory gains stock that never left the seller's pool — phantom availability that buyers and the price resolution can see.
items.design: Credit inventory only for quantity that actually clears (matched + auto-cleared), or defer the inventory credit until after the auto-clear pass resolves which orders held. Guard with an order_book_harness assertion: a held order leaves mc.inventory unchanged for that resource. Decide whether the supply-side price signal should still see held stock (an argument exists both ways — held stock is real and near the market, but it is explicitly not for sale below its floor); default to NOT visible, matching the reservation semantics BL-386 established.
items.resolution:
Landed 2026-08-16, Sprint 19. The listing-time credit in market_clearing.cpp is deleted; market_component::inventory is now credited inside each of the three statements that debit a pool — the auto-surplus clearing loop, the matched-trade debit loop, and the auto-clear pass (se.rem, floor <= resolved only). Inventory gains exactly what pools lose, expressed as a conservation law rather than a tally so the two cannot drift apart in a later edit.

WHY IT WAS MORE THAN A PRICING NICETY. market_component::inventory is not a display field: economy_system.cpp draws processor inputs from it (run_processing coverage and consumption, and run_construction). A held order credited stock no seller had parted with, so a processor bought that phantom stock, decremented it, and no counterparty was ever paid — goods from nothing AND money destroyed, the same family as BL-351 over-listing.

GUARDED by order_book_harness R7 (12 rows), beside BL-386 R6 hold rows it extends: held credits nothing; a clearing order credits exactly its pool loss; the auto-surplus path likewise; a MIXED tick with one held and one clearing order against the same (market, resource) credits only the clearing half — the row that a per-resource rather than per-order credit would fail; and a matched explicit trade plus its auto-cleared remainder credit once between them. Three of the twelve (R7.2, R7.3, R7.10) were confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix build before the fix was accepted, so the guard discriminates rather than merely passing. order_book_harness 64/64.

A SIDE EFFECT WORTH NAMING: the old credit iterated the sell books in unordered_map order, accumulating floats in an unspecified sequence. All three new sites are ordered (std::map pools, sorted market and resource keys), so the credit is now deterministic as well as correct.

MEASURED NEUTRAL WHERE IT SHOULD BE (NR-263): ai_skill_harness is byte-identical across all five benchmark seeds before and after, and spectator_determinism is unchanged — the AI places standing orders in those worlds but none of them hold, so the benchmark never reached the defect. econ_harness, econ_stability, econ_bankruptcy, market_inventory_harness, procurement_harness, market_emergence_harness, corp_ai_harness, build_spree_harness, trade_routes_harness, world_determinism and determinism_harness all green; the whole Lua-free suite was swept and its only failures (ai_skill stale GCC bands, spectator R2 pre-BL-409 golden, history_sim 5 rows) are pre-existing and identical before and after.

SCOPED OUT, both recorded rather than dropped: held stock stays visible to the supply-side price signal against the item design own default, because deciding a hold FROM the resolved price which is computed FROM supply is a fixed point (NR-261, with the asymmetry written into MARKETS.md); and an explicit matched trade still delivers to the shared market shelf rather than the buyer stockpile, which is dormant until BL-160 gives the buy side a verb (NR-262).

items.title: Chain depth is the growth track — how far down the production graph a corp can reach is what gates its next building
items.summary: RULING 2026-08-15 (Ben, elicitation form): the growth track's spine is CHAIN DEPTH, not building tiers, not the tech ladder, not settlement scale. A corp advances by reaching further down the production graph - the goods it can actually make gate the buildings it may place next - so growth is a consequence of the economy it has built rather than a parallel unlock system laid over it. This is the item the roster expansion (BL-429) and the alternate methods (BL-430) both hang from, and the structure tech (BL-296) and politics (BL-158) are meant to REFINE rather than replace.
items.design:
FILED 2026-08-15 from Ben's sprint-planning ruling. Four spines were offered - building
tiers, chain depth, the ancient tech ladder, settlement scale - and chain depth was taken.

## What the ruling means

Growth is not a separate track. A corp's reach down the production graph IS its progress:
the deeper the chain it can close, the more the world opens to it. Concretely, a building's
placement precondition becomes a statement about goods the corp can already produce, rather
than a flag some other system sets. Build a bloomery, and the smithy becomes placeable
because blooms exist; not because a tech completed.

Why this over the alternatives, in Ben's choice and worth recording: a tier ladder or a tech
ladder is a SECOND system that must be kept in agreement with the economy, and the project
has already paid that reconciliation cost once (BL-155/BL-156 both settling on the same
`condition_set` and neither building it). Chain depth has no second system to desync from -
it is read off the recipe graph that has to exist anyway.

## Why this is the right substrate right now

The ancient arc's resource enum is ALREADY stocked for it and mostly idle. `components.hpp`
carries stone, timber, sand, clay, peat, charcoal, iron_blooms, grain, fodder, salt and
bullion - the BL-286 logistics tranche plus the ambient raws - and BL-286's own comment
admits the behaviours were never filed ("behaviour unfiled" appears five times). Several
carry no base price in `world_gen.lua`, which is exactly the minable-but-unsellable asymmetry
BL-340 closed for the space tier and never closed for the ancient one.

So the depth ladder does not need new resources. It needs the chains that consume the ones
already sitting in the enum. That is the cheapest possible version of this feature and the
most honest: it retires orphans instead of minting them.

## What has to be defined

1. **A depth metric.** Depth of a good = longest input path back to a raw. Computed once at
   registry load from `recipes.lua`, not authored per good, so it cannot drift from the graph.
   Determinism: the graph is authored data, the walk is pure - it must produce the same
   number on every toolchain (the BL-406 lesson: never let an unordered container decide a
   number the economy reads).
2. **What depth gates.** First cut: building placement. A building type declares the minimum
   depth its corp must have REACHED (i.e. actually produced at least once, recorded per corp),
   and `placement_rules.cpp` enforces it alongside terrain.
3. **Cycles.** The graph must be acyclic for depth to be defined. The registry load should
   reject a cyclic recipe set loudly rather than looping - a headless harness assertion.
4. **What "reached" means for a corp** - produced once ever, or currently producing? Produced
   once ever is the legible choice (progress does not evaporate when a building idles) and
   costs one per-corp bitset over resource_type.

## Guard

A headless harness (`tools/verify/chain_depth.cpp`) asserting: the graph is acyclic; every
good's depth is stable across two loads; every building's declared minimum depth is
REACHABLE from the starting position (no unplaceable building, the roster equivalent of an
orphan resource); and that a fresh corp can reach the deepest tier by some path.

## The refinement seam this leaves open

Tech (BL-296) and politics (BL-158/v0.1.6) refine this rather than gate it: a tech can make a
chain cheaper, shorter, or unlock an ALTERNATE method (BL-430) for a chain you already run -
it does not hand you a depth you did not earn. Stated here so the later systems have a shape
to attach to instead of re-litigating the spine.
items.resolution: Complete 2026-08-16 (slice 2; slice 1, the metric, landed 2026-08-15 with BL-429/430/431). The gate: recipe_required_depth (a recipe's deepest input, derived in the same bounded fixed point as depth_of so it cannot drift from the graph or the era mask), corporation_component::produced_ever + corp_reached_depth (produced-once-ever, never cleared — progress must not evaporate when a building idles), mark_produced at the two sites a good is genuinely made, and refusal at BOTH doors: construct_building and try_switch_recipe. Guarding only placement would have left a one-click bypass (place the shallowest method, retool to the deepest sibling), so the gate is applied at the retool path too; both map to corp_command_result::rejected_depth_locked so the seam cannot tell them apart. ANCIENT ROSTER ONLY per Ben's 2026-08-16 ruling, with the band check on the RECIPE — an any-band recipe stays ungated even in an ancient campaign, so no existing industrial campaign changes shape. Build door filters locked methods out; the Method page disables the Switch with a plain-language reason rather than a depth integer. Guard: chain_depth G1-G4 (11 assertions), including BL-432's no-stranded-building row — the ancient ladder climbs to depth 3 with nothing stranded. Doc: PRODUCTION.md § The gate. Found en route and fixed: the Build door passed a browse recipe index as an absolute id (NR-254), a latent wrong-recipe bug in exactly the ancient campaigns this work targets.

items.title: The building roster is 7 types and half of them are space-era — the ancient arc needs 20+ buildings that consume the resources it already has
items.summary: RULING 2026-08-15 (Ben): take the roster past 20 building types, as a content sprint of its own. Measured today: scripts/economy.lua carries SEVEN building_type entries (extraction_site, processing_facility, port, launchpad, inland_logistics_hub, military_base, research_institute) and scripts/recipes.lua carries 17 recipes, one per output. Named buildings like the Hydroponics Bay and Fishing Wharf are not types at all - they are the generic processing_facility distinguished by recipe and placement rule, which is the pattern the expansion should follow rather than minting enum values.
items.design:
FILED 2026-08-15 from Ben's sprint-planning ruling ("20+ types, content sprint of its own").

## What is actually there today

  * building_type entries in `economy.lua` : 7
  * recipes in `recipes.lua`               : 17, one per output, no alternates
  * of the 7 types, LAUNCHPAD is space-era and the refinery chain runs on PETROLEUM

The arc is the ancient product at 0 CE (NR-177). A roster expansion that adds to the current
set without confronting that would double the space-era debt inside the live product - see
BL-433, filed alongside this, which owns the misplacement question.

## The pattern to follow, and the one to avoid

BL-166/BL-168 established it and `economy.lua` records it: the Hydroponics Bay and the Fishing
Wharf are the SAME `processing_facility` / `extraction_site` types as everything else,
distinguished by recipe and by placement rule, not by a new enum value. That is how a roster
reaches 20+ named buildings without a 20-value enum, without touching the serialised width,
and without a glyph explosion.

**Mint a new `building_type` only where BL-325's test is met** - it earns the enum value with a
distinct placement rule AND a distinct glyph AND behaviour no recipe can express. The
military_base passed that test. A tannery does not.

## What the roster should cover, against the resources that already exist

The enum already holds the ancient substrate: stone, timber, sand, clay, peat, charcoal,
iron_blooms, grain, fodder, salt, bullion, plus the endemic four (tobacco, spices, coffee,
furs). Most are BL-286 orphans - in the enum, unconsumed by any recipe, several unpriced in
`world_gen.lua`. The roster's job is to give every one of them a consumer, which is BL-340's
admission rule applied to the ancient tier:

  * **Extraction** - quarry (stone), clay pit, sand pit, woodcutter (timber), peat cutting,
    salt pan, grain farm, pasture (fodder), mine (iron ore, copper ore)
  * **Primary processing** - charcoal burner (timber -> charcoal), bloomery (iron ore +
    charcoal -> iron_blooms), kiln (clay -> ceramics), glassworks (sand -> glass),
    sawmill (timber -> timber goods), mill (grain -> flour/rations)
  * **Secondary** - smithy (blooms -> tools/arms), tannery, weaver, potter, shipwright,
    stonemason
  * **Terminal / mercantile** - mint (bullion), warehouse, market stall

That is comfortably past 20 named buildings on ~3 building_type values. Exact list, recipes
and magnitudes are the sprint's content work; the ADMISSION RULE is the invariant - no
building whose output nothing consumes, no resource no building consumes.

## Depth, and how this item relates to BL-428

Every entry above declares its minimum chain depth (BL-428). The roster IS the depth ladder
made concrete: quarry at depth 0, bloomery at 1, smithy at 2, and so on. Build the ladder and
the roster in the same pass or the numbers will not agree.

## UI consequence, which is half the work

20+ buildings will not fit the Build door's current shape, and ICONS.md gains a glyph per
named building. Both are in scope: a roster the player cannot browse is not content, it is a
data file. Its question_log entry must be written with it (BL-260).

## SLICE 1 LANDED 2026-08-15 — the chains, not yet the named buildings

What landed: the ancient production chains and the prices that make them tradeable. What did NOT:
the named building identities (quarry, woodcutter, kiln, smithy...), their placement rules and
glyphs, and a Build door that can present 20+ entries. Requirements `ancient-chain-roster` R1-R4
complete, R5-R6 pending.

**The measurement that justified doing it this way round.** Before this slice the ancient arc's max
chain depth was **1** — one layer above raws and nothing beyond. Named buildings on top of a flat
economy would have been 20 ways to do the same shallow thing. Depth first, identities second.

**The load-bearing edit was a RETAG, not the five additions.** Tagging the coal-fired `steel` recipe
`industrial` is what gave the ancient arc depth. With the shallow coal route still available (coal is
a raw), BL-428's min-across-recipes rule correctly collapsed steel back to depth 1 — the new chain
would have existed and meant nothing. Ancient max depth went 1 -> 3 on exactly that change. Worth
remembering as a general shape: adding a deep chain does not deepen an economy while a shallow route
to the same good remains open.

**A trap this slice created and closed in the same pass.** Three call sites defaulted an
unconfigured processing facility to `recipe_id("steel")`. That still RESOLVES after the retag — the
storage path is band-independent by design (BL-433) — so an ancient campaign would have silently
seeded its processors with an industrial recipe, and nothing would have refused it, because the era
gates browsing and placement rather than execution. Now `default_recipe_id()`. The general rule, and
it is worth stating because the next author will hit it: **ask the registry for a sensible default;
do not name a recipe and hope.**

**A latent defect found on the way** (NR-237): `resource_from_name` was missing eight BL-286 enum
values despite its own comment claiming full-enum coverage, so any recipe naming one threw at load.
Invisible until now because BL-286 shipped those goods with their behaviours "unfiled", so nothing
ever authored against them.

**Still orphaned**, and recorded rather than glossed: `sand` and `peat` are priced by this slice but
consumed by nothing. BL-432 is where that becomes a mechanical assertion.

## SLICE 2 LANDED 2026-08-15 — named identities, sand/peat closed, peat_cutting gap fixed

Built: a `recipe::display_name` field (recipe_registry.hpp/.cpp), authored for the five slice-1
ancient recipes (Charcoal Burner, Bloomery, Smithy, Potter & Weaver, Miller) and shown by both the
Build door (selection_panel.cpp) and the live-building method selector (construction_panel.cpp) in
place of the raw recipe key / the old "Processing: X" prefix. An `extraction_building_name()` lookup
does the same for extraction rows (Quarry/stone, Woodcutter's Camp/timber, Sand Pit, Clay Pit, Peat
Cutting, Iron/Copper Mine, Water Extractor, Coal Mine, Oil Field, Silica Quarry, Rare-Earth Mine),
plus Farm vs Fishing Wharf now read as distinct names rather than sharing one "Extraction:
Agricultural Produce" label. `display_name` defaults to a title-cased recipe name when unauthored, so
every recipe (industrial included) has a legible label with nothing new to author.

**R6 closed**: sand and peat, "still orphaned" per slice 1, now each have a consumer — Glassworks
(sand -> trade_goods_misc) and Peat Kiln (peat -> charcoal), recipes 22/23. Both are a second producer
of an existing output from a different raw, the same multi-producer shape `steel` already has
(coal-smelter / iron-nickel / bloomery), not BL-430's alternate-method feature.

**A real pre-existing gap found and fixed on the way**: `placement_rules::k_extractable` never
listed `resource_type::peat`, despite tile_generation.cpp authoring peat deposits on wetland tiles —
no extraction_site could ever have targeted it. Fixed by adding it to the array; `buildings_rework_harness`'s R1 (`n >= 15`) still holds at 16.

**Ancient-band Build-door count**: with the additions, an ancient campaign on a resource-rich tile
can show up to ~9 named extraction rows + 9 named processing rows (2 any-era + 7 ancient recipes) +
4 infrastructure rows (Port/Hub/Military Base/Research Institute, all any-era) — comfortably past the
R5 threshold of 20+.

**Deliberately NOT done this slice, and recorded rather than glossed** (the remainder of R5):
**per-building glyphs.** Icons still render per `building_type` (`icons::building` switches on
`extraction_site`/`processing_facility`/...), so every named extraction building shares one ore-chunk
glyph and every named processing building shares one square — exactly how Farm/Smelter/Hydroponics
Bay already render today, not a regression. Giving 16 ancient buildings each a silhouette-distinct
hand-drawn glyph (ICONS.md's own "Adding a new glyph" process, one at a time) is real asset-authoring
work this slice did not attempt; a follow-on item should own it explicitly rather than R5 quietly
passing without it. See NEEDS_REVIEW.json for the decision record.

**Also recorded**: this slice's C++ changes (recipe_registry.hpp/.cpp, placement_rules.hpp,
selection_panel.cpp, construction_panel.cpp) were authored and manually re-reviewed but NOT
compiled — the remote session's network policy denies `codeload.github.com` (SDL3/sol2/ImGui
FetchContent sources), a 403 confirmed as an organization policy denial, not a transient fault. Lua
changes (recipes.lua) were syntax-checked with `luac5.4 -p` and pass. A compile + the existing
headless/visual harnesses are owed at the next session with real toolchain network access.

## SLICE 3 LANDED 2026-08-15 — R5's glyph clause closed (NR-239)

`icons::building()` gained a fourth parameter, `resource_type identity`: an extraction
site's target resource, or a processing facility's PRIMARY OUTPUT (the new shared
`primary_output_resource()`, moved from construction_panel.cpp into recipe_registry.hpp so
every UI file draws the same identity). 14 new hand-drawn glyphs cover the 9 extraction +
5 processing resource keys the ancient roster reaches — Quarry, Woodcutter's Camp, Sand Pit,
Clay Pit, Peat Cutting, Iron Mine, Copper Mine, Water Extractor, Farm/Fishing Wharf, and (for
processing) the charcoal-kiln, bloomery, ingot, goods-bundle and ration-pack shapes. Two or
more named buildings reaching the same resource share one glyph BY DESIGN (documented in
ICONS.md § 1c): the glyph says what a building makes, not which recipe, so Charcoal Burner/
Peat Kiln (both -> charcoal) and Potter & Weaver/Glassworks (both -> trade_goods_misc) read
the same — exactly as two Iron Mines on different tiles already share a glyph.

All four `icons::building()` call sites updated: the Build door (selection_panel.cpp), the
Buildings-tab identity plate (construction_panel.cpp), the on-canvas marker
(body_surface_canvas.cpp — the target/recipe lookup was hoisted OUT of the wrap-copy k-loop,
since the pre-existing under_construction pattern it was modelled on only resolves at k==0
and would have shown the wrong glyph on every wrap copy of a non-default-resource building),
and the placement ghost preview (extraction-only — armed placement mode carries no recipe
field to key a processing ghost on).

requirements.json's `ancient-chain-roster` group is now ALL SIX rows complete (R1-R6).
BL-429's own status stays `designed` rather than flipping to `complete`, deliberately: see
NR-241 below.

items.title: A building has a recipe, not a choice of one — alternate production methods with real trade-offs
items.summary: RULING 2026-08-15 (Ben): yes, alternates with real trade-offs - not tier upgrades. Today recipes.lua is one recipe per output and a building stores a single recipe id, so choosing a building IS choosing its method. An alternate is a different input basket for the same output, each honestly better under different conditions (local abundance, chain depth, wage cost, throughput), so the player is choosing rather than upgrading.
items.design:
FILED 2026-08-15 from Ben's sprint-planning ruling ("yes, alternates with real trade-offs" -
chosen over "only as tier upgrades" and over keeping one recipe per output).

## The distinction the ruling turns on

A **tier upgrade** is strictly better and therefore not a decision - it is a delay. An
**alternate** must be genuinely better under some conditions and worse under others, or the
player will find the dominant one once and never look again. That is the design bar, and it
is testable: if any alternate dominates its sibling on every axis, it is a tier, not a method,
and the pair should be re-authored or merged.

## The trade-off axes available today

Real ones the engine already has, so no new machinery is needed to make the choice bite:

  * **Input basket** - charcoal vs peat vs coal as smelting fuel: what is locally abundant
    differs by body and region, so the same method is not best everywhere.
  * **Labour intensity** - `base_wage` and workforce against `base_rate`: a hand method is
    cheap to build and dear to run; a water-powered one inverts that.
  * **Chain depth** - a deeper method needs a good you may not reach yet (BL-428), so the
    shallow method stays correct early and stays available late.
  * **Throughput vs yield** - batches per tick against output per batch.

## Shape

`recipes.lua` entries gain a `produces` / method grouping so several recipes can declare the
same output and be presented as siblings. The recipe id stays the 0-based index and ORDER
MUST STAY STABLE - authored ids are stored in `building_component.recipe` and a reorder would
silently repoint every existing building. Append new methods; never insert.

Switching method on a running building is the existing recipe-switch path (BL-079's reflex
already switches a floored recipe), so the mechanism exists - what is new is that the choice
becomes the player's, with a cost or a cooldown to switch so it is a commitment rather than a
per-tick optimisation. That cost is a first-cut constant in `economy.lua`, tuned by playtest.

## Guard

A headless harness assertion that no method DOMINATES a sibling on every axis
(inputs cost, wage, rate, depth) - the mechanical form of the design bar above. It will need
a price snapshot to compare input baskets, so it belongs next to the existing economy harness.

## Interaction with the AI

`corp_ai.cpp` scores build/demolish/survey/road/hire. Method choice is a NEW decision surface
and the scorer will pick badly by default (it has no notion of local abundance). Either the
alternates are scored - a small, deterministic addition in the same scored-utility layer - or
background corps are pinned to the shallow method explicitly. Pinning silently is the failure
mode: it would make every rival look strategically identical. Decide at promotion; either way
it is a stated call, not a default.

items.title: The production choice and the chain that leads to it have no surface — method selector, chain trace, and the depth readout
items.summary: The UI half of the economy-breadth sprint. Three surfaces the player needs the moment BL-429 and BL-430 land: a production-method selector on the building panel (with the trade-off legible at the point of choice, not after), a chain trace answering "what do I need to make this", and a depth readout answering "how far down the graph have I actually got". Without these the content is invisible: 20+ buildings and a choice of method are a data file the player cannot see.
items.design:
FILED 2026-08-15 with the economy-breadth sprint. This is the "pad out the UI" half of
Ben's ask, applied to the economy side; BL-393's unit surfaces are its military twin.

## Three questions, three surfaces (BL-260 discipline - each declares the question it answers)

1. **"Which way should this building make its output?"** - a method selector on the Selection
   panel's building view. Shows each alternate's input basket, wage and rate SIDE BY SIDE, so
   the trade-off (BL-430) is legible at the point of choice. A selector that shows only names
   pushes the player to a wiki. Switching cost shown before committing, like the Build door
   shows a credit total.
2. **"What do I need in order to make this?"** - a chain trace from any good back to its raws,
   reachable from the good itself (resource pip, market row, recipe line). Read off the same
   registry graph BL-428 computes depth from, so it cannot disagree with the simulation.
3. **"How far down the graph have I actually got?"** - the depth readout: the corp's reached
   depth, what the next depth would open, and what is missing to get there. This is the growth
   track made visible, and without it chain depth is an invisible gate that reads as a bug.

## Constraints

The Selection panel is already dense; the method selector must not push the workforce dial or
profitability off screen. Rule 0b applies at build time - state the current measurements
before reshaping the panel, and open the live app before asking Ben to judge the layout.

Toggle rule applies to any ledger slot this earns.

## Owed alongside the code

  * `docs/ui/question_log.json` entries for all three surfaces, written WITH them, not after.
  * `docs/ai/ACTIONS.json` - method switching is a new control and therefore a new dictionary
    entry. Transcribed from the seam verb once it exists (BL-270 discipline), never authored
    ahead of it.
  * A user story per surface in `user_stories.json`: the intent axis has nothing on "choose how
    I produce" today.

items.title: The live ancient product still ships a Launchpad and a petroleum refinery — the roster contradicts the arc
items.summary: Found 2026-08-15 while sizing the economy-breadth sprint. The live arc is the ancient product at 0 CE (NR-177), but scripts/economy.lua still carries a launchpad building_type and scripts/recipes.lua still refines petroleum into refined_fuel and propellant. Not a bug - it is the space arc's roster, correctly parked at the version level but never parked in the DATA the ancient product loads. A player at 0 CE can be offered a launchpad.
items.design:
FOUND 2026-08-15 while measuring the roster for BL-429.

## What is there

`economy.lua` § buildings carries `launchpad` as one of seven building_type entries.
`recipes.lua` id 1 is petroleum -> refined_fuel, and the BL-308 propellant recipes sit on top
of it. The space arc is parked at the ROADMAP/backlog level (~41 items carry `parked: true`),
but parking was a backlog operation and the Lua data was not part of it.

## Why it matters more than it looks

Three ways it bites, in order of how much:

1. **The player at 0 CE can be offered a launchpad.** Whatever the placement rules do in
   practice, the roster is what the Build door reads, and an anachronism there reads as a bug
   in the product rather than a parked feature.
2. **BL-429's roster count is measured against a polluted baseline.** "Seven building types"
   includes one that should not be in this arc at all - so the real ancient roster is six.
3. **The AI scorer sees them.** `corp_ai.cpp` scores build candidates over the roster it is
   given; a rival that builds toward a space chain in an ancient world is not a strategy, it
   is a data leak.

## The call this needs

Not mine to take, because it decides how the two arcs share one data set:

a) **Era-gate the data** - each building and recipe declares the era it belongs to; the
   loader filters on the campaign's era. Truest, and ERAS.md already designs an era system
   (status: designed, NOT implemented), so this would be its first real consumer.
b) **Split the data files** - `economy_ancient.lua` / `economy_space.lua`, chosen at startup.
   Cheapest, and honest about the two arcs being two products; costs duplication where they
   genuinely overlap (extraction_site, port, warehouse).
c) **Leave it and rely on placement rules** - the status quo. Cheapest of all and the reason
   this was invisible until now.

RECOMMENDATION: (a). It is the same amount of work as (b) once, it gives ERAS.md its first
implementation instead of leaving it a designed-but-unbuilt doc, and the ancient arc's own
tech ladder (BL-296) will want an era-ish gate anyway. But it is a shared-substrate decision
and BL-429 should not start before it is answered - the roster expansion writes into exactly
these files.

## RULING 2026-08-15: option (a), era-gate the data

Taken on Ben's instruction to answer this myself and start Sprint 17. Reasons unchanged from
the recommendation: (a) and (b) cost about the same once, (a) gives ERAS.md its first
implementation instead of leaving it a designed-but-unbuilt doc, and BL-296's ancient tech
ladder will want an era-shaped gate anyway. (b) additionally duplicates every entry the two
arcs genuinely share — extraction_site, port, warehouse — and duplication is what goes stale.

## The trap that shapes the implementation

A recipe's **id is its index** in `m_recipes`, and that id is STORED in
`building_component.recipe`. So the era filter must be a MASK, never a removal: dropping a
disallowed recipe from the vector would silently repoint every building whose recipe sat
after it. `recipes.lua`'s own header already says "keep the order stable so authored ids
hold" — the filter has to honour that.

The shape that satisfies both, without touching the ten call sites that iterate recipes:

  * `m_recipes` keeps EVERY authored recipe, in file order. `get_recipe(id)` and
    `recipe_id(name)` stay absolute — they are the storage/lookup path.
  * A new `m_allowed` vector holds the positions permitted in the current era.
    `recipe_count(bt)` / `recipe_at(bt, i)` map through it — they are the BROWSE path, and
    every existing caller already means "the recipes available to me" by them.

That split is why no consumer needs rewriting: the ten sites that walk
`[0, recipe_count)` start walking the era's recipes instead of all of them, which is what
each of them was already trying to express.

## Band, not era-number

Two bands plus a wildcard: `any` / `ancient` / `industrial`. Deliberately NOT reusing
ERAS.md's Era 0 / Era 1 numbering — that axis is about *space access within the industrial
arc* and is gated on launchpad presence, a different question from *which product is this*.
Conflating them would give one field two meanings.

The campaign's band is derived from `world_params::epoch_year` against the SAME 1700
threshold the antiquity branch already documents, so there is one number in the codebase and
not two: below 1700 is ancient, 1700 and above is industrial.

## Default is 'any', and that is load-bearing

An unset registry permits everything, so every existing headless harness — none of which
knows about eras — loads exactly the roster it loads today. Same property BL-409 relied on
for spectator mode: the new behaviour is opt-in, so the un-opted path is byte-identical and
can be asserted as such.
items.resolution: Landed 2026-08-15, option (a). `era_band` (any/ancient/industrial) tags every authored building type and recipe; the campaign's band is derived from world_params::epoch_year against the 1700 threshold and set in app::load_economy. The filter MASKS rather than removes, which is the whole shape of the change: storage (get_recipe/recipe_id) stays absolute so stored recipe ids never repoint, while browse (recipe_count/recipe_at) walks the era's list — and because every existing caller of the browse path already meant 'the recipes available to me', none of the ten call sites needed rewriting. construct_building is the authoritative gate (construction_result::era_locked, distinct from tech_locked because no research reaches it, surfaced as corp_command_result::rejected_era_locked rather than overloading rejected_placement — BL-395's complaint); the Selection build door filters on building_available so it does not offer what the gate would refuse. Default band is `any`, so every pre-existing harness and the default world are untouched. Guard: tools/verify/era_roster.cpp, 15 assertions ALL PASS, live-Lua and script-rooted. Docs: PRODUCTION.md gained an era-band section (incl. the storage/browse table); ERAS.md's header block gained the note that this is a SECOND thing in code saying 'era' and is a different axis from Era 0/Era 1. Ancient roster is deliberately thin (steel, food_rations, refined_copper) — filling it out is BL-429.

items.title: processing_facility does the job of every kind of processing — split it into recognisable sub-facility groups
items.summary: Raised 2026-08-16 during the BL-431 building-card playtest: Ben noticed switching a building's recipe (BL-430) could switch it to a recipe with nothing in common with its current one — a Bloomery becoming a Loom by picking from a dropdown. Filed and landed same session: every recipe gains a `group` ("Metal Foundry", "Food Processing", ...), the Build door offers one candidate per group rather than one per recipe, and cross-group switching is refused outright rather than priced (a same-session retraction of an initial tiered-cost design — see resolution).
items.design:
FILED 2026-08-16 mid-playtest. Ben: "Now is also the time to implement the building splits, so
Processing Facility doesn't just do the job of every type of processing, allowing simple
splits. It should also cost money for any building to undergo a large change, making it in
some cases cheaper to just build another."

First cut: add `recipe::group`, tag every recipes.lua entry, collapse the Build door's
per-recipe processing rows into one row per group, and price a cross-group recipe switch at
a steep multiplier (`cross_group_multiplier`, first-cut 6.0x) on top of BL-430's existing
switch cost — cheap to retool within a group, expensive enough to often favour building fresh
across groups.

## RETRACTION, same session

Ben reconsidered after the priced version landed: "I didn't realise that switching methods
can mean changing to a different building type — we should retire that completely. So the
only way to access a different building type is fully dismantling the building, then using
the tile selector to reselect and build a new building." Cross-group switching is not merely
expensive now, it does not exist: `try_switch_recipe` refuses a cross-group target outright
(`recipe_switch_result::cross_group`, mutates nothing), the Method page's candidate list only
ever offers same-group recipes (never shows what it would refuse), and
`cross_group_multiplier` was removed rather than left unused. Dismantle + rebuild via the
tile selector is the sole route to change a building's group.
items.resolution: Landed 2026-08-16 across two passes in one session (price-tiered, then retracted to refuse-outright — see design). Group taxonomy: Metal Foundry, Refinery, Food Processing, Chemical Works, Electronics, Advanced Fabrication, Welfare Goods, Fuel Production, Artisan Goods (docs/economy/PRODUCTION.md § Sub-facility groups has the full recipe table). Two taxonomy judgment calls (Hydroponics Bay's group; the merged Advanced Fabrication group) logged as NR-252, open. Guard: tools/verify/recipe_switch_harness.cpp S6a-f assert the refusal path (cross-group switch declined, recipe unchanged, nothing debited); S1-S5 (BL-430's original mechanism) and R1 (the pre-existing no-dominance finding, NR-243) untouched. Build door (draw_construction_ledger) collapses per-recipe processing candidates to one row per group, seeded with the best-expected-profit recipe in that group.

Landed 2026-08-16 as the R1/R2 rows of tools/verify/chain_depth.cpp, completing the item — its third assertion (every building's minimum depth reachable) had already landed as G3 with BL-428's gate, and the first (acyclicity) as D4. R1 (no orphan resources, either direction) SHIPS RED on eight resources and is left that way deliberately: five (grain, fodder, salt, transport_capacity, bullion) are orphaned in both directions and are exactly the BL-286 'behaviour unfiled' values this item's own design predicted, reproduced independently rather than asserted; three more (platinum_group_metals, regolith, machinery) are obtainable but unconsumed. Content decision logged as NR-257.
