weeks. The lesson is that the surface half must be its own tracked item, not a task inside
the model item where it is the first thing cut under pressure.

## Shape

The Corporation panel gains a stance column and the three presses, gated on visibility.
A stance toward a corp the player has not discovered is not shown — the BL-068
competitor-visibility rule applies, and *whether someone has declared war on you* is not
obviously public information. **That is a second question for Ben** and is smaller than the
symmetry one: does a declaration announce itself, or is it discovered on contact? It rides
naturally on the comms dock if it announces.

Presses issue `corp_command` records. Declaring hostility takes a confirm popup on the
demolish precedent — it is not literally irreversible, but under Reading A it is not
unilaterally reversible either, which is close enough to warrant the friction.

## Owed alongside

A `question_log.json` entry, and `ACTIONS.json` entries for the new verbs — transcribed
from the seam after it exists, never authored ahead of it (BL-270 discipline).

items.title: Rivals need to score a stance change as an ordinary candidate
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17. The reasoning half of the friend/neutral/hostile model - rivals choosing stance on the existing deterministic scored-utility layer, with no new planner and no nation behaviour.
items.design:
## The constraint first

This is a widening of the BL-202/BL-203 exception in exactly the way BL-324 (rival hiring)
was: one more legal verb family on the same deterministic scored-utility layer. It is
**not** a diplomacy planner, has no negotiation state machine, and adds no nation
behaviour — nation actors stay deferred, and stance is corp-to-corp only.

Every term below must be pure, seeded and replayable, computed from world state a rival
can legitimately see under BL-068.

## The scoring terms

**Toward hostile.** Score rises with contested overlap — shared bodies, shared market
bodies, competition for the same scarce resource — and with the relative-strength read
`compute_corp_standings` already produces. It falls with the target military capacity and
with the fraction of the scorer own income that flows through markets the target also
sells into. A corp does not open a war it is losing, and does not burn a market it eats from.

**Toward friendly.** Score rises with complementarity: the target sells what this corp
buys, and their build focuses do not collide. This is where BL-446 (scorer procurement)
composes — a supplier you have completed contracts with is the natural friend, and
`corp_reputation` is already the scalar that says so.

**Toward neutral.** The de-escalation term, and the one most likely to be forgotten.
Without it stances ratchet and every long game ends with everyone hostile to everyone.

## Hysteresis is required, not optional

Stance changes must carry a margin the way the workforce and recipe dials do. A stance
that flips on a marginal score is worse than no stance model, because it makes the
Decision Feed unreadable and makes any downstream military trigger fire on noise. One
stance command per corp per evaluation, and a cooldown before the same pair may move again.

## Legibility

New `corp_decision_reason` values so the Decision Feed reads *why* a rival declared. This
is the item main payoff under spectate: a spectated war whose cause is invisible is a
fight, not a story.

items.title: The spectator harness cannot see a verb the scorer never emits
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 from the Sprint 22 audit. spectator_determinism buckets the 15 verbs into four families (build / dial / survey / trade / other), so seven verbs no scorer emits are absorbed silently by families their siblings satisfy.
items.design:
## The blind spot

`family_of()` maps `place_sell_order`, `remove_sell_order`, `request_quote`,
`accept_quote` and `cancel_contract` all to `verb_family::trade`. A rollout in which
rivals place sell orders and do nothing else satisfies the trade family completely, and
the four unemitted verbs beside it are invisible. The same absorption hides `demolish` and
`place_road` inside `other`, which `hire_unit` satisfies on its own.

So the harness that exists to prove spectate exercises the seam proves it at a granularity
too coarse to notice that seven of fifteen verbs never fire.

## Shape

Keep the family assertion — it is doing a different job (BL-409 R1, that no single corp
needs all four families over a short run). **Add** a per-verb histogram over the rollout,
printed always and asserted never. A printed count is the right instrument here: asserting
a floor per verb would fail legitimately whenever a verb is correctly rare, and a harness
that fails legitimately is a harness that gets muted.

The histogram is then the behavioural half of BL-444 (verb coverage tool) static read —
one says the path exists, the other says it was walked.

## Cheap and independent

One file, no world change, no golden movement. It should run first in any reachability
work, because it is the measurement everything else is judged against.

items.title: The convoy layer is the largest built subsystem with no player verb at all
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 from the Sprint 25 logistics audit. Layer 5 - convoy component, terrain-weighted A* routing, the km-per-tile travel-time model, road/river/node discounts, four rendering paths and a persistent trade-route store - is entirely automatic. None of the fifteen corp_verbs names a convoy. SUPPLY.md's own Build status has carried the line 'Player-directed dispatch (the Dispatch trigger exception has no UI or code path yet)' since the layer landed, and its Dispatch trigger section describes player-direction as a shipped exception that was never built.
items.design:
## The gap, measured

`corp_verb` holds fifteen values. Eight name a building, three an order, two a
contract, one a body (`survey`), one a tile (`place_road`). **None names a convoy.**
`dispatch_convoys` is called from the economy tick and from nowhere else; the only
way a player influences a lane is indirectly, by building a port or a road and
hoping the auto-dispatcher notices.

This is the same defect BL-393 (units are write-only and inert) describes one layer
over, and it is larger: the convoy layer is ~340 lines of `supply_system.cpp` plus
the whole of `logistics.cpp`, and it is the *only* coupling between two markets'
prices. SUPPLY.md § Convoy entity states it outright - "there is no abstract
price-coupling term between bodies: the convoy *is* the coupling". The player cannot
touch it.

**Sprint 22's reachability audit could not see this.** It joined seam, dictionary,
surface and scorer over the verbs that exist, and every one of the fifteen is
reachable from at least one direction. The question it did not ask is which
*subsystems* own no verb. Recorded as NR-308.

## Shape - two verbs, not a routing UI

**`dispatch_convoy`** (subject = source market, `target` = resource, `quantity`,
`counterparty` = destination market). Commits cargo from the source pool at once,
exactly as the auto path does, prices the haul through the same `intra_body_path` /
`body_distance_au` call, and appends a `convoy_component`. It is the auto-dispatcher's
body with the shortfall scan removed - **no second code path**, which is the same
mitigation Sprint 22 named for BL-445.

**`hold_convoy`** (subject = convoy). Not a cancel: cargo already left the pool, so
a cancel would have to invent a return leg or mint goods. A held convoy stops
advancing and pays nothing further; releasing it resumes. The narrow version is
the honest one - a full recall is a separate design question and is out of scope here.

Both go through `apply_corp_command` and are refused, not clamped, on a bad field:
the seam is an untrusted input boundary (standing rules, 2026-08-14), so quantity is
range-checked against the source pool as the value that lands, and a rejection
mutates nothing.

## What this deliberately does not add

No waypoint routing, no standing lane orders, no per-node throughput (SUPPLY.md puts
that out of prototype scope), no convoy escort. Escort is the interesting one and it
belongs after BL-315 (conflict spine) and BL-448 (stance) - a convoy cannot be escorted
until something can threaten it.

## Dictionary

Two new `gameplay` family entries in ACTIONS.json, **transcribed from the seam once it
exists** and never authored ahead of it (BL-270's discipline). This is also the first
time the dictionary will carry a verb whose subject is a transient entity, which is
worth getting right: a convoy id is valid for a handful of ticks.

## Why this minor

v0.1.12 (logistics modes) is themed *"distance costs something, in more than one way,
and the player can see it"* and carries four items - freight premium (BL-153), rail
(BL-173), coastal ports (BL-188), supply-lens flow (BL-175). Every one of them makes
distance cost more or read better. **After all four land, the player still cannot
dispatch a convoy.** This item and BL-453 are what turn that minor from a tuning pass
into a lever.

items.title: In-flight convoys are drawn on three canvases and listed nowhere
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 from the Sprint 25 logistics audit, and filed separately from BL-452 on purpose. Convoys render well - a moving beam with a trailing tail on the Planetary canvas, inter-body lines on the Solar canvas, a convoy glyph under the Supply lens, an aggregated trade-route graph under Supply-routes. What no surface gives is the list: what is in flight, carrying what, from where to where, arriving when, and at what haul cost. A player can watch a convoy and cannot read one.
items.design:
## Why separate from BL-452

BL-350 (procurement seam) landed complete world state, serialisation, validation and a
harness with **no player surface at all**, and nobody noticed for weeks - Sprint 22's
audit found it. A surface that is a task inside the model item is the first thing cut
under pressure. So the press is its own item, blocked on the seam, and the two are
argued against the same behaviour.

## The surface

A **Convoys tab on the Market Ledger**, beside Sell Orders and (per Sprint 22's BL-445)
Contracts. Same chrome, same toggle rule, no new ledger slot on the nav rail.

One row per in-flight convoy of the player's corp: cargo resource and quantity, source
and destination market, mode glyph (land / sea / space - air is never dispatched), a
progress bar off `convoy_component::progress`, **ticks to arrival** derived from
`speed`, and the haul cost already paid. Selecting a row focuses the lane on the active
canvas; the Hold press (BL-452's second verb) sits on the row.

The dispatch press itself belongs on the **market Selection card**, not here - a
dispatch starts from a source you are looking at, and the ledger is the register of what
is already moving.

## The number worth showing that nothing shows today

`ticks to arrival`. The travel-time model landed 2026-08-12 and is genuinely load-bearing
- a long haul now takes several quarters where it used to take one - and **no surface
reports it**. A player who cannot see arrival time cannot feel the change the model made,
which makes it the strongest single argument for this tab.

## Question log

Required, per BL-260: the question is *"what is on its way to me, and when does it land"*.
Drafted rather than settled - Ben's wording.

> ⟳ 2026-08-19 (N1 audit): Re-labelled: LANDED, AWAITING VERIFICATION (bd71143) — not open, do not re-build. Compile-by-inspection favourable (every field read exists in components.hpp:674-705). To close: integrating build (MSVC 14.44), a scripts/verify/convoys.lua (NEW check — naming it in verifier-visual needs Ben's permission; can run as a one-off), the live Hold press per the 2026-08-19 rule, and NR-323's question_log wording once seen. R7 (spectator byte-identity golden) is a SEPARATE pre-existing Windows re-bless owed by the whole Sprint 25a batch — do not conflate.

items.title: An army is bought once and then is free forever - w.units appears in no economic flow
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 from the Sprint 25 audit, code-verified: `w.units` is referenced in economy_system.cpp, budget_system.cpp and construction.cpp exactly zero times. hire_unit debits a one-off resource draw plus a credit cost (BL-394) and after that a regiment is free in perpetuity, while every building beside it pays maintenance and wages every single tick. SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, answering NR-306): upkeep is BOTH - credits AND military goods (supplies, rations, weapons). That is reading (c), the largest of the three offered, and it makes upkeep a physical draw on the logistics network rather than a line in the budget.
items.design:
## The measured state

`grep w.units` across `economy_system.cpp`, `budget_system.cpp` and `construction.cpp`
returns nothing. `apply_budget`'s five flows (income / expenditure / maintenance /
wages / interest - FINANCE.md) are **all building-derived**. `operating_cost` takes a
`building_component`. There is no unit pass anywhere in the economy tick.

So the standing rules' concern about rival hiring - BL-324's "never on cash" for
availability, and Ben's 2026-08-13 ruling that spending is still gated by solvency -
currently prices only the **moment of hire**. A rival that hires twelve units carries
no recurring burden for them, which means the solvency gate it passes at hire time is
the only pressure the roster ever applies.

**The second half of the same gap: `demolish_building` erases the asset, the building
and its stockpile, and never touches `w.units`.** Demolishing a military base silently
orphans every unit mustered there - BL-393 names this and the code confirms it
(`construction.cpp`, the three erase calls).

## SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, on NR-306): reading (c) - credits AND goods

The question was credits (a), goods (b), or both (c). **Ben's answer: both - credits and
military goods (supplies, rations, weapons).** This is the largest of the three and it is
the one that makes the item what its title claims: an army that costs something is an army
that *draws on the network*, not one that debits a number.

Three consequences follow immediately, and none of them are optional under (c):

**1. The cost is a VECTOR, not a float.** The unit pass resolves, per unit type per tick,
a credit wage plus a set of `{resource_type, qty}` draws against the corp's pool **on that
unit's body**. Written as a float-plus-extras it becomes a rewrite the first time a second
good is added; written as a vector from the start the roster carries the data and the pass
carries no per-good knowledge at all.

**2. A pool can be empty, so there is a partial-supply case, so there is a shortfall rule.**
This is the part reading (a) did not have. When the goods are not there the unit must do
*something*, and the honest options are strength decay, desertion (count attrition), or
combat-effectiveness reduction. **Decay is the right one and it is already designed** -
BL-325 S3 is out-of-supply decay, authored as a deterministic scalar in economy.lua with no
RNG. Under (c) the two items converge: S3's decay fires when the unit is beyond the reach
field, this item's fires when the goods did not arrive, and they are the same subtraction
from the same field for the same reason. **Land one decay rule with two triggers, not two
rules.**

**3. The goods have to exist, and one of them does not.** See § The roster gap below.

## The roster gap - there is no military good in the game

Audited against `resource_type` (37 values, RESOURCES.md):

| Ben's word | Nearest existing value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **rations** | `food_rations` (22) | **exists**, produced from agricultural produce, already consumed by the consumer-goods recipe |
| **supplies** | `medical_supplies` (36) | **exists but is wrong** - it is a *habitability* good consumed by population centres, and borrowing it would make an army compete with a city for medicine on a shared price. Defensible later; not what "military supplies" means |
| **weapons** | *nothing* | **ABSENT.** No ordnance, no small arms, no munitions anywhere in the enum |

So (c) cannot be built as stated without a new terminal good. That is **BL-457**, filed
alongside this item, and this item `requires` it.

The finding is larger than a missing enum value. The 2026-08-10 refocus (NR-120) put the
player's identity as *"a national private militia, which uses private companies to build
equipment"*, with trade *"coloured directly with military use"*. BL-350 gave procurement a
terminal good to contract for and it is `spacecraft_components` - **space hardware. There
is no military terminal object in the roster at all.** The refocus's other half has been
an assertion since the day it was made.

## Slices

**U0 - the good.** BL-457 lands ordnance and its recipe. Blocking; nothing below works
without a good to draw.

**U1 - the unit pass.** A pass over `w.units` in the economy tick, deterministic, iterated
in sorted unit-id order. Resolves the per-type cost vector from the roster, debits credits
and goods, and records the shortfall. Orphan cleanup rides here: a unit whose owning corp
no longer holds a completed military_base on its body is the demolish defect's fix, and the
pass is the only place that can see it.

**U2 - the flow.** Upkeep as its own term in `apply_budget`'s decomposition, not folded
into wages - the budget ledger reads the split and a hidden term is a term nobody tunes.
The goods half is a pool debit, not a budget flow, and shows in the stockpile ledger.

**U3 - the shortfall rule.** One decay rule, two triggers, shared with BL-325 S3 (see
consequence 2 above). Deterministic scalar, no RNG.

**U4 - the surface.** Upkeep on the unit Selection card - credits and the goods vector,
with the unmet part called out - and a force line in the budget ledger. A cost the player
cannot see is a cost they cannot respond to, and under (c) there are now two ways to fail
to pay it.

## The check

A `unit_upkeep` harness asserting: (1) a corp with N units pays exactly N x the type's
credit rate and debits exactly N x each good, and nothing else moves; (2) an empty pool
produces decay at the authored scalar and never negative stock; (3) demolishing the base
leaves no orphan unit; (4) two runs of one seed produce identical balances, pools and
strengths; (5) **the rate-zero run is byte-identical to the pre-item build** - the same
defaults-off proof `spectator_determinism` used for BL-409, and the thing that makes the
golden re-bless honest.

## Risk

This touches `economy_system.cpp` and `economy.lua`, which Sprint 21's own risk paragraph
names as the hot seam. It **moves every economy golden**, because every seed with a hiring
rival now spends differently, and under (c) it also moves every *pool*. Take the
measurement of how far rival balances and stocks move before raising the rate off zero.

**Reading (c) roughly doubles (a)'s cost and adds a genuine design surface** (the shortfall
rule). It is the right answer for what the item is trying to do; it is not the cheap one,
and it should not be promoted as though it were a one-session job.

## Correction to this item's first draft

The 2026-08-17 filing said the goods half was *"the grain/fodder line BL-287 has been
holding"*. Both halves are wrong: BL-287 is a verify-harness item, the logistics-goods item
is **BL-286**, and grain and fodder were **removed** from the enum by NR-257 on 2026-08-16
as produced-by-nothing/consumed-by-nothing. The stale citation was inherited from BL-325's
own design prose, which still carries it (BL-295 fixed the same citation in components.hpp
and did not reach the backlog copy). Recorded as NR-311.

items.title: military_points is deleted and science is wired to the tech gate - two write-only accumulators, resolved differently
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 from the Sprint 25 audit. BL-332 gave every completed military_base a per-tick credit to corporation_component::military_points and every completed research_institute a credit to ::science. A full grep across src/ finds three sites for each: the declaration, the Lua param load, and the write. No gate reads them, no surface shows them, no scorer scores them, and the AI blackboard does not export them. They accumulate forever and mean nothing.
items.design:
## Same shape as the orphan resources

NR-257 removed five `resource_type` values that were produced by nothing and consumed by
nothing. These two are the mirror: **produced by something and consumed by nothing.** The
precedent is the point - the roster got healthier by deleting rather than by finding uses,
and the same test should be applied here rather than assumed away.

`military_capability_harness` verifies the accumulation faithfully - symmetry across player
and non-player corps, no credit while under construction or decommissioned. It is a green
check over a number nothing reads, which is the Sprint 18 lesson in a different key.

## This is a measurement first, not a build

Do not design a consumer before asking whether one is wanted. The item's first output is
the answer to one question per accumulator:

- **`science`** most likely has a home: `tech_gate.cpp` exists and BL-344 landed one earned
  tech. If the tech ladder's unlock currency is meant to be this field, the gap is a wiring
  job and the item is small. If the ladder is gated some other way, the field is redundant.
- **`military_points`** is the harder one, and the honest answer may be **delete**. Under
  BL-325 the economy->military interface is the base tile plus the reach field, and under
  BL-454 the recurring cost is credits and goods. A third abstract military currency beside
  those either gates something (what?) or duplicates them. If BL-094's governing-body pivot
  wants it, it is a v0.3.0 field arriving three minors early.

## Either outcome is a result

Wire it or remove it. What is not acceptable is a third state where it keeps accumulating
and a future reader assumes it means something - the exact failure the orphan resources
caused. If it is removed, the harness rows go with it and the removal is a save-format
change (BL-107's magic header is the thing that would reject a stale save).

Recorded as NR-307.

## SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, on NR-307): delete `military_points`, wire `science`

The item was filed as a measurement — wire it or remove it, and do not leave a third state.
Ben answered per accumulator, and the two answers differ, which is the outcome the item was
shaped to allow.

### `military_points` — **delete**

It has no home. Under BL-325 the economy→military interface is the base tile plus the reach
field; under BL-454 the recurring cost of force is credits and ordnance. A third abstract
military currency beside those either gates something nobody has named or duplicates them.
If BL-094's governing-body pivot later wants a military capacity scalar, it is an **append
with its behaviour filed in the same change** — the standing rule, unchanged, and the exact
discipline NR-257 enforced on the resource roster.

**What goes with it:** the field, the `military_points_per_base_tick` param and its Lua
row, the write in `economy_system.cpp`'s per-tick pass, and
`military_capability_harness`'s military half. **The research half of that harness stays**
and becomes the science wiring's check.

**Note this is a save-format change** in the same sense BL-457's append is: it changes
`corporation_component`'s layout. Free today, not free once BL-107 lands.

### `science` — **wire it to the tech gate**

`tech_gate.cpp` exists and BL-344 landed one earned tech, so the currency and the consumer
are both already present and simply not connected. This is a wiring job, not a design:
`science` accumulates as it does today and the gate spends it.

**One thing to settle while wiring, and not to invent:** whether a tech's cost is *spent*
(balance decrements on unlock) or *reached* (a threshold the total must pass). Read BL-344's
landed shape and match it rather than choosing freshly — the tech that already exists is the
authority on which model the ladder uses.

### Why the split answer is the right one

The precedent that shaped this item — NR-257 — deleted five values rather than finding uses
for them. It would have been easy to apply that uniformly and delete both. The difference is
that `science` has a **consumer already written and waiting**, and `military_points` has
a consumer nobody can name. That is the test, and the two fields fail it differently.

items.title: The military layer has no authority doc, so eleven items point at the AI doc or at nothing
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 from the Sprint 25 audit. docs/ has economy/, generation/, ui/, ai/, lore/, tech/ and development/ - and no military/. BL-325 (military bases and supply) names docs/ai/AI_OPPONENT.md as its authority, which is the doc about the rival's decision-making, not about how force works. The battle resolvers, the terrain scalars, the roster, the reach-as-supply ruling and the unit model are spread across campaign_battle.hpp, combat.hpp, terrain_combat.cpp, unit_roster.cpp and eleven backlog items, with no doc that owns the subject.
items.design:
## Why it matters here rather than as tidying

CLAUDE.md's § Documents is a **traversal map** - the instruction is to find the doc that
owns the question and read that, because the corpus is ~650K tokens and reading it all
stopped being possible. The military subject has no entry in that map. A session asked to
work on units, supply decay or a battle trigger has nowhere to start and reads source, which
is how Sprint 21's audit found that BL-315's resolver was *already built* while three sprint
blocks in a row described it as unbuilt.

That is the concrete cost, and it has already been paid once.

## What the doc owns

Written as an authority for what is **built**, in the SUPPLY.md style - a status banner and
a Build status section separating landed from outstanding, so it cannot rot into an
aspiration doc:

- The two resolvers and the difference between them: `resolve_battle` (Era -1, nation-scale,
  called by the history sim) and `resolve_campaign_battle` (campaign-scale, seeded rounds,
  priced withdrawal, **zero callers**).
- The unit model: `unit_component`'s five fields, tile-canonical position (BL-157), and the
  `strength` fixed-point inconsistency NR-247 is still open on.
- The roster and its era bands; the corp-side gate.
- The muster interface: `military_base`, hire-at-base, and BL-325's ruling 3 - one reach
  field, economic equals military - which is the single most load-bearing military decision
  taken so far and currently lives only in a backlog item's `design` field.
- Terrain defence and attrition scalars.
- What is absent and known to be: hostility (BL-448), unit verbs (BL-393/BL-314), engagement
  trigger, battle state in the world, upkeep (BL-454), out-of-supply decay (BL-325 S3).

## Mechanical tail

Add the § Documents entry to CLAUDE.md, and repoint the `authority_doc` field on the military
items that currently name AI_OPPONENT.md. Both are small; the doc is the work.

## Not in scope

This writes down what exists and what is known missing. It does **not** settle hostility,
the symmetry question (BL-448/NR-302), or anything Sprint 21's audit lists as absent - a
doc that decides open design questions on the way past is how authority docs get ahead of
their work, which DELIVERY.md § Design state prohibits.

items.title: The militia has no military good to buy - ordnance does not exist in the roster
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17, falling out of Ben's answer to NR-306 (unit upkeep draws credits AND military goods - supplies, rations, weapons). Audited against the 37-value resource_type enum: food_rations exists, medical_supplies exists but is a habitability good consumed by population centres, and WEAPONS DO NOT EXIST - no ordnance, no munitions, no small arms anywhere. The wider finding is that BL-350 gave procurement a terminal good and it is spacecraft_components; there is no military terminal object in the roster at all, which leaves half the 2026-08-10 militia refocus as an assertion.
items.design:
## The gap

The 2026-08-10 refocus (NR-120) reads: *"a national private militia, which uses private
companies to build equipment for space. So the flavour of trading is initially coloured
directly with military use, and space equipment."* **Military use and space equipment.**
The space half landed - BL-340's chain terminates in `spacecraft_components`, which BL-350's
procurement contracts buy. The military half has no object. A player cannot buy a weapon
because there is no weapon.

This went unnoticed because nothing consumed one. BL-454 (unit upkeep) is the first consumer,
which is also what makes the value admissible now and not before.

## The admission rule is satisfied, which is the whole argument

PRODUCTION.md / BL-340's rule: *a value earns its place by being consumed by an authored
recipe or contracted for by a named actor, and nothing else gets in.* NR-257 enforced it by
removing five of BL-286's values that met neither test twelve days after they were added.

`ordnance` meets both: **consumed** by BL-454's unit pass every tick a unit stands, and
**contracted for** by procurement the moment it exists. It is also a natural terminal for a
chain that currently only terminates in space hardware.

## Shape

**One value, appended.** `ordnance = 37`, `count = 38`. Appended at the end, never inserted -
the enum is serialised and every per-resource array is sized off `count` (the BL-308
save-format note). Re-reading that note: an append is free today because no save layer exists,
and stops being free when BL-107 lands.

**Deliberately ONE value, not three.** Ben's words were "supplies, rations, weapons", and the
temptation is a value each. Resisted: `food_rations` already covers rations and is already
produced, and "supplies" without a distinct consumer is exactly the produced-by-nothing shape
NR-257 deleted. One new value with one clear consumer beats three with one between them. If
the upkeep vector later wants a distinct field ration or a medical draw, that is an append
with its behaviour filed in the same change - the standing rule, unchanged.

**Recipe.** Fabricator, `steel + machinery -> ordnance`, which places it at the same chain
depth as `alloys`/`electronics` and makes it a real growth-track object under BL-428's depth
gate rather than something a starting corp can make on tick one. An ancient-era route
(`iron_blooms + charcoal`) belongs with BL-429's ancient roster, not here.

**Base price** authored in the same change, as BL-286's cautionary precedent requires.

## What it unblocks beyond BL-454

- **Procurement gets a military object.** `request_quote` for ordnance is the militia's own
  contract, and it needs no new seam - BL-350's verbs already take a `resource_type`.
- **The trade-is-coloured-by-military claim becomes mechanical.** A market with a war in reach
  prices ordnance differently, which is the first time conflict has ever moved a price.
- **BL-458 (interdiction) gets cargo worth taking.** A convoy carrying ordnance to a hostile
  corp's front is a target with a reason, not a generic freight loss.

## The check

`chain_depth`'s R1 row (no orphan resources) is the guard that would have caught this good's
absence of a consumer, and it is the row that must stay green after the append - so BL-454's
consumer and this value should land in the same batch, or R1 goes red in between.

items.title: A convoy cannot be intercepted - the logistics network is invulnerable to force
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 on Ben's rescope steer. Nothing in the game can stop a convoy. Cargo moves from dispatch to arrival with no interaction with units, stance, terrain control or force of any kind - the logistics layer and the military layer share a world and touch nowhere. This is the item that makes supply lines a military object, and it is the reason BL-454 (upkeep) matters: an army that draws on the network gives an enemy something to cut. SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, on NR-310): cargo is CAPTURED - credited to the interceptor's pool at the interception body - with destruction as the fallback when it cannot be credited.
items.design:
## Why this is the payoff item and not a nice-to-have

BL-454 makes an army draw goods along the network. BL-452 lets a player direct a convoy down
a lane they chose. Neither means anything against an opponent until the lane can be **cut** -
without that, logistics is a cost model and the military layer is a separate game played on
the same map.

It also gives BL-315's own ruling its mechanic. That item settled that **army, mercenary and
pirate are three derived readings of one company** - *the reading is derived, never authored*.
Army and mercenary have paths to being read (BL-377's contracts, a hostile stance). **Pirate
has no mechanic at all**: there is nothing in the game a company can do that would make
"pirate" the honest reading of it. Interdicting a convoy is exactly that act. The naming rule
has been waiting since 2026-08-07 for the verb that earns the third reading.

## The finding that makes this cheap: a convoy already has a position

`convoy_component` stores no path and no tile, which reads at first like interdiction needing
new state. It does not. `body_surface_canvas.cpp` already derives the full tile path per
convoy from `source_market` -> `centre_tile`, `dest_market` -> `centre_tile` and
`intra_body_path`, then interpolates a head along it by `progress`. That derivation is
**deterministic, already cached, and already correct** - it is how the beam renders.

So the work is to move it out of the renderer:

```
entity_id convoy_tile_at(const world& w, const convoy_component& cv);
```

in `logistics.hpp`, returning the tile the convoy's head occupies (or `null_entity` for an
inter-body leg in transit). The canvas then **consumes** the shared function instead of
owning a private copy - which also removes a live duplication, since the renderer's version
would otherwise drift from the world's.

Caution: the canvas copies and conditionally reverses the cached path (`if (st != std::min(st,
dt)) std::reverse(...)`) because `intra_body_path` caches on a canonicalised key. The shared
function must own that orientation rule, or a convoy's head lands at the wrong end of the
lane half the time - a bug that would be invisible on screen (the beam looks fine either way)
and fatal to interdiction.

## Shape

**The trigger.** In the economy tick, after `advance_convoys` and before
`credit_arrived_convoys`: for each convoy, resolve `convoy_tile_at`; if that tile carries a
unit whose owner is **hostile to the convoy's corp** under BL-448's stance table, the convoy
is intercepted. Deterministic, sorted iteration, no RNG in the detection - the roll, if any,
belongs in the resolver, not the trigger.

**Not a battle by default.** A convoy is cargo, not a force. The first cut resolves an
interception as an *outcome*, not as a round-by-round engagement: unescorted cargo meeting a
hostile unit is taken or destroyed. Escort - a unit assigned to a convoy, turning interception
into a real `resolve_campaign_battle` call - is the obvious follow-on and is deliberately not
in this item. It needs BL-315's engagement machinery to be *shipped* rather than merely built.

**Stance is the predicate and the only predicate.** No incidental interception by neutrals, no
terrain-based blockade, no ambient banditry. Hostility is a declared state a corp opts into
(Ben, 2026-08-17, the BL-448 ruling) and interception is one of the things it then permits -
which is also what stops this from being a random tax on trade.

## SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, on NR-310): CAPTURE, with destruction as the fallback

Cargo leaves the source pool at dispatch (SUPPLY.md § Convoy entity), so the goods are
already committed and either answer conserves. Ben chose capture.

**The rule.** On interception the cargo credits the interceptor's `(corp, body)` pool at
the interception tile's body. If it cannot be credited — no pool reachable at that body —
it is destroyed instead, and the outcome says which happened. An interceptor with no market
access holds goods it cannot sell, and that is a legitimate outcome that is **not**
special-cased away.

**Why it matters beyond flavour.** The corp AI is a deterministic scored-utility layer that
prices candidates by payoff. Destroy-only gives an interception a payoff of zero to the
interceptor and a cost in exposure, so BL-450's stance scorer would correctly never rank it
— interdiction would ship and only ever fire when the *player* did it, which is the same
unreachable-capability defect this whole sprint exists to fix. Capture gives the scorer a
number.

**And it earns BL-315's third name.** That item settled that army, mercenary and pirate are
three derived readings of one company, *derived and never authored*. A company that takes
cargo reads as a pirate. One that only burns it reads closer to a saboteur.

**The conservation assertion follows from this and is the harness's load-bearing row:**
captured quantity in == quantity credited, exactly, with the destroyed-fallback path
asserting zero credited and zero minted. No path may create goods.

## Surfaces

An interception is the single most consequential thing that can happen to a player's economy
without them pressing anything, so it cannot be silent: a comms-dock message naming the lane,
the cargo and the interceptor, the convoy's row leaving BL-453's Convoys tab with a stated
cause rather than vanishing, and the interception tile marked on the canvas for a few ticks.
A `question_log.json` entry per surface, per BL-260.

## The check

An `interdiction` harness: (1) `convoy_tile_at` agrees with the renderer's derivation on every
lane in a generated world, in both key orientations - the orientation bug above is the one this
item is most likely to ship; (2) a hostile unit on the head tile intercepts and a neutral one
does not; (3) goods are conserved exactly under capture and exactly destroyed under destroy -
no minting either way; (4) two runs of one seed intercept the same convoys on the same ticks;
(5) an interception with no stance table entry never fires.

## Sequencing - this item is gated and says so

`requires` BL-315 (units must be commandable and standing somewhere on purpose), BL-448 (stance
is the predicate) and BL-452 (a player-directed convoy is the thing worth cutting; auto-dispatch
alone makes interdiction happen *to* the player with no counterplay). **It cannot start before
Sprints 21 and 23 land.** That is the cost of the rescope and it is stated rather than hidden.

items.title: unit_component::strength duplicates count, and nothing converts a unit into an army_stack_entry
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 resolving NR-247 and NR-300 together, on Ben's ruling. unit_component documents strength as a 'Fixed-point combat strength scalar' and BOTH writers set it to the same value as count (corp_command.cpp:472-474 hire_batch_manpower, corporation_generation.cpp:1606-1608 starting_unit_manpower), so today it is a literal duplicate of the headcount and both readers print it raw. Separately, both battle resolvers take fully-resolved army_stack_entry values and no adapter converts a live unit into one. Ben's ruling: make strength genuinely fixed-point, driven by roster type quality AND supply state.
items.design:
## Two entries, one cause

NR-247 (2026-08-13) recorded that `strength` is documented as fixed-point while every
writer sets it raw. NR-300 (Sprint 21 audit) recorded that nothing converts a
`unit_component` into an `army_stack_entry`, and observed that NR-247's ambiguity had
therefore stopped being cosmetic and become blocking. They are the same item: the adapter is
the thing that has to decide what `strength` means, and it has been deferred three times
because nothing needed the answer yet.

**A sharper reading than either entry recorded.** `unit_component` carries `count` *and*
`strength`, and both writers set them to the **same value**:

```
.count    = hire_batch_manpower,   // corp_command.cpp:472
.strength = hire_batch_manpower,   // corp_command.cpp:474
```

So this is not an ambiguously-scaled field. It is a **duplicate**, with two writers keeping
two copies of one number in sync by hand and nothing enforcing it.

## SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben): genuinely fixed-point, driven by type quality AND supply state

The options were delete the field, keep it raw and fix the comment, or make it real. Ben
chose real, and then chose what makes it diverge from `count`:

```
strength = count × roster_type_quality × supply_factor        (×100 fixed point)
```

**`count` stays the headcount.** It is the honest thing and other systems read it as one.

**`roster_type_quality`** comes from `unit_roster` — the per-type scalar that makes a
heavy unit worth more than a levy at equal headcount. The roster already keys per type; this
gives that key a combat meaning it did not have.

**`supply_factor`** is the load-bearing half and the reason this item sits in the same
sprint as BL-454. When the upkeep pass cannot pay a unit's ordnance and rations draw, the
shortfall reduces `supply_factor`, and therefore reduces `strength`, and therefore
reduces what the resolver reads. **That is the whole military-logistics coupling arriving in
combat rather than staying in the budget.** An unsupplied army does not merely cost less to
run — it loses.

It also means BL-325 S3's out-of-supply decay and BL-454's shortfall rule and this factor are
**one mechanism seen from three places**, which is the consolidation Ben's reading (c) already
implied. Land them as one rule.

## Scale, and the one trap

**×100**, so a 50-man levy at quality 1.0 and full supply reads 5000. `strength` is already
`int32_t`, so headroom is not a concern.

**The trap: `strength` must stop being stored as an independent writable field, or the
duplicate problem comes straight back.** Either it is *derived on read* from
`count × quality × supply_factor`, or it is a stored cache with exactly one writer (the
economy tick's unit pass) and no other site permitted to set it. **Derived is correct here** —
there is no cost to computing it, and a stored copy is what created this defect.

So the change is: `unit_component` keeps `count` and a `supply_factor`, **drops the
stored `strength`**, and gains a free function `unit_strength(w, unit)` that computes it.
The three writers stop writing it; the two readers call the function.

## The adapter, which is the reason any of this is urgent

```
army_stack_entry unit_to_stack_entry(const world& w, const unit_component& u);
```

in `combat.hpp`'s neighbourhood, feeding `resolve_battle` and
`resolve_campaign_battle`. Both resolvers deliberately never look a roster up — they take
resolved values — so this function is the *only* place the roster meets combat, and it is the
single seam Sprint 21's audit named as missing.

Write it here, with the strength model, rather than inside BL-315: BL-315 is about commanding
units and triggering engagements, and if the adapter lands there it lands as an
implementation detail chosen under time pressure. NR-300's own warning is precisely that.

## The doc comment

Delete the current one. It has been wrong since the struct shipped and it is what made two
sessions believe a divisor existed. Replace it with the formula above, and MILITARY.md
(BL-456) carries the long form.

## The check

Extend `combat_harness` or add a `unit_strength` harness: (1) two units of equal count and
different roster type produce different strengths, in the right order; (2) an unsupplied unit
produces strictly lower strength than a supplied one of identical composition; (3) the adapter
round-trips a unit into a stack entry that the resolver accepts, and two runs of one seed
produce identical entries; (4) with quality 1.0 and full supply, `strength == count × 100`
exactly — the calibration anchor that keeps the fixed point honest.

## Sequencing

`requires` BL-457 (ordnance must exist before a supply factor can measure its absence).
Pairs with BL-454 — the upkeep pass is what writes `supply_factor` — and unblocks BL-315's
adapter slice. Independent of stance and interdiction.

items.title: Ordnance cannot be produced at the shipped epoch - the only military good is masked out by its own era tag
items.summary: Found 2026-08-18 by Sprint 26b's doc truth pass and confirmed against source. BL-457 (ordnance) added the game's only military terminal good with a Fabricator recipe tagged era = "industrial" (scripts/recipes.lua id 27, line 450). era_band_for_epoch (recipe_registry.hpp:36-38) returns era_band::ancient for any epoch_year < 1700, and the shipped default epoch is 0 CE. So the good BL-454 (unit upkeep) draws every quarter CANNOT BE MADE in the product as it ships.
items.design:
## What was found

Confirmed by reading source, not inferred from a doc:

- `scripts/recipes.lua:450` — the Fabricator ordnance recipe carries `era = "industrial"`, tagged under BL-433 (space-era buildings in the ancient arc).
- `src/world/recipe_registry.hpp:36-38` — `era_band_for_epoch` returns `era_band::ancient` whenever `epoch_year < 1700`.
- `src/world/hard_coded_world.hpp` — the default campaign epoch is 0 CE.
- `src/world/construction.cpp:47` and `src/world/economy_system.cpp:728` both gate on the ancient band.

An ancient campaign therefore masks out the only route to `ordnance`.

## Why this is worse than a missing recipe

BL-457 (ordnance) was admitted to the roster under PRODUCTION.md's standing rule that a new resource needs a consumer, and BL-454 (unit upkeep) was that consumer. The consumer shipped. The **producer is unreachable at the epoch the product actually runs at**.

It is currently masked by the upkeep rates all being 0.0. **The moment NR-321 turns the rates on, an ancient army draws a good nobody in the world can make.** That makes this a blocker on the rate rollout, not a content nicety.

Same epoch mismatch as BL-461 (campaign roster band is industrial), one layer down. Both are the 0 CE refocus not having reached the data files.

## The author knew, and that is the real lesson

`scripts/recipes.lua:445-447` says so outright: *"NO ANCIENT ROUTE HERE. An iron_blooms + charcoal path is a real idea and belongs with BL-429's ancient roster, not smuggled in beside an industrial-era recipe."*

That was the right call. The wrong part is that **no item was filed for the ancient route**, so a deliberate deferral became an invisible gap — the exact shape NR-257 deleted five resources over.

## The fix, and the call it needs

The recipe comment already names the shape: an `iron_blooms + charcoal` ancient route at an ancient building. Which building is BL-429's (ancient building roster) to say.

**Open question for Ben:** does ordnance get an ancient route now — small, and it unblocks NR-321 — or does the ancient arc get a *different* military terminal good, leaving ordnance industrial?

## The guard that should have caught it

`chain_depth`'s R1 row asserts no orphan resources, and BL-457 was given an explicit R1 exemption naming BL-454 as its consumer. R1 checks a consumer **exists** — not that producer and consumer are reachable **in the same era band**. Making R1 era-aware is the durable half of this item, and it generalises: any future era-tagged recipe can strand its own output the same way.

## CLOSED 2026-08-19

**Ben's ruling on the open question:** add an ancient route now, do not invent a second military terminal good — ordnance stays the one military terminal good across both eras.

**The route.** `scripts/recipes.lua` id 28, `ordnance_from_blooms`: `era = "ancient"`, `group = "Metal Foundry"`, `display_name = "Smithy"` — the SAME building as id 19's steel recipe (`iron_blooms + charcoal`), not a new one, per the task's own instruction to reuse the roster rather than invent a fourth ancient metalworking building. Same quantities as the steel recipe (2 iron_blooms + 1 charcoal), so switching the Smithy between "make steel" and "make ordnance" is a straight BL-430 alternate-recipe swap rather than a new resourcing decision. `ordnance`'s `base_price` (43.0, BL-457) is unchanged.

**The guard.** `tools/verify/chain_depth.cpp` gained an **R1b** row: per concrete campaign band (ancient/industrial), is a resource WANTED there (a recipe consumes it in-band, or a named actor-consumed exemption applies — narrower than R1's own table, restricted to actor consumers with a REAL per-tick/contract stockpile draw verified against source, since tobacco/spices/coffee/furs/trade_goods_misc have no programmatic drain at all and would false-positive) but not REACHABLE there (no recipe produces it in-band, no deposit yields it)? Verified PRE-fix: reverting the recipe addition and rebuilding reproduces the exact failure (`STRANDED: resource id 37 (ancient)`); restoring it returns the harness to `ALL PASS (0 failures)`, 34/34 assertions.

**Five known, tracked, OUT-OF-SCOPE gaps of the same shape** surfaced by R1b (spacecraft_components, propellant, clean_water, consumer_goods, medical_supplies — all industrial-only-produced, all drawn by consumers that are not era-gated in the C++) are recorded in R1b's `k_known_gaps` table and filed as **NR-355** rather than silently fixed or silently passed — fixing five more goods was not this item's stated scope (a single-good, difficulty-2 fix).

**Docs updated:** `docs/economy/PRODUCTION.md` (§ Fabricator's "no ancient route" claim corrected; § The ancient chain gained the Smithy's second recipe row) and `docs/economy/RESOURCES.md` (§ The two terminal goods gained the BL-460 paragraph). Full project build (`ProjectIo` target) confirmed clean alongside the harness.

items.title: The campaign roster band is hard-coded to industrial in a 0 CE product
items.summary: unit_roster.hpp:61 sets campaign_roster_band = roster_band::industrial, with a comment still reading "The 1960s campaign's fixed roster band" — against a default epoch_year of 0. Bands are cumulative, so ancient rows are still offered; the defect is that INDUSTRIAL rows are offered too. A 0 CE mercenary company can hire industrial-era units, and corp_ai can score and hire them. Three call sites read the constant and none consults the epoch. [COMPLETE 2026-08-19: campaign_roster_band_for(era_band) replaces the hardcoded industrial constant at all three call sites (selection_panel.cpp, corp_ai.cpp, corp_command.cpp), deriving from recipe_registry::era(). campaign_roster_band.cpp harness 12/12 PASS. MILITARY.md corrected.]
items.design:
## What was found

`src/world/unit_roster.hpp:55-61` declares `campaign_roster_band = roster_band::industrial`, above a comment reading *"The 1960s campaign's fixed roster band (BL-324, 2026-08-08) … the campaign is simply industrial-era throughout, and bands are cumulative"*.

That comment was true the day it was written. The 0 CE refocus landed 2026-08-12 (NR-177) and moved the default epoch to 0. **This constant did not move with it.**

Read by three call sites, none of which derives it from the epoch: `src/ui/selection_panel.cpp:2656`, `src/world/corp_ai.cpp:1303`, `src/world/corp_command.cpp:421`.

## Why priority A rather than cosmetic

The problem is *not* that ancient units are unavailable — bands are cumulative, so they are offered. It is that **industrial rows are offered as well**, to the player's hire surface *and* to `corp_ai`'s hire scorer.

So the shipped ancient product currently lets a 0 CE mercenary company field industrial-era units, and lets a rival score and hire them under the BL-324 exception. That is a content-correctness defect in what ships today, not a latent one.

## The fix

Derive the band from the epoch, reusing `era_band_for_epoch` (`src/world/recipe_registry.hpp:36-38`) rather than introducing a second era concept.

**The roster and the recipe registry should agree by construction.** The existing split between them is precisely how BL-460 (ordnance unproducible at 0 CE) also happened — two independent notions of "what era is this" drifting apart.

BL-274 (era-keyed unit rosters) is the neighbouring item and carries NR-080's open question on how a band gets chosen. This item is the narrower correction and should **not** wait on it.

## Assertion owed

A harness row asserting no roster row above the epoch's band is ever offered. That is the check that makes this class of drift visible, instead of needing a doc-truth pass to stumble on it a week later.

items.title: Every Era -1 harness measures a 4000-year six-band run; generation ships a 400-year one-band run
items.summary: Found 2026-08-18 when Sprint 27's BL-384 agent and Sprint 26b's doc agent reported contradictory facts, and both turned out to be right. history_sim_params defaults to 4000 BCE -> 0 CE across a six-band clock costing 136 decision rounds (history_sim.hpp:126-140). Production overrides all of it: hard_coded_world.cpp:531-536 sets start_year = epoch_year - prehistory_years (0 - 400 = -400), tick_bands[0] = {epoch_year, 4}, tick_band_count = 1 — a 400-year run on one 4-year band, 100 rounds. Every harness takes the struct default, so no check in the project measures the run that actually generates a world.
items.design:
## The divergence, verified

| | span | clock | decision rounds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `history_sim_params` default (every harness) | 4000 BCE → 0 CE | six bands, 100→50→20→10→5→1 | **136** |
| Production (`hard_coded_world.cpp:531-536`) | 400 BCE → 0 CE | one band, 4 years | **100** |

A **10× difference in span** and a different clock shape. `history_sim_harness`, `history_sweep` and the Ages view all read the struct default; only `make_hard_coded_world` overrides it.

## Why this is priority A

**It silently invalidates the instruments the whole Era −1 arc is about to be steered by.** Sprint 27 committed a red conquest assertion measured on the 4000-year ladder. Its findings — the bimodal fight/no-fight split, the Settle-vs-Campaign pricing gap, and the elimination arithmetic — are all measured against a configuration that does not ship.

This is the third instance of this repo's recorded failure mode: Sprint 18 found a visual check pointed at a deleted tab; Sprint 18b found `player_seed_sweep` timing out and never once passing. Both were *checks that looked like coverage and were not*. This is the same shape at the config layer, and it is larger, because it affects **every** Era −1 check at once.

## The consequence that matters most

The BL-384 agent's H2 argues elimination is **arithmetically** unreachable: one verb per polity per round × 136 rounds caps whole-era conquest at 136 provinces, against powers holding ~119–180. **Production has 100 rounds, not 136** — so the ceiling is *tighter* in the shipped world, and the argument gets stronger rather than weaker. But the province counts under a 400-year settlement pass are unmeasured, so the ratio is unknown. **Measure it on the production config before Sprint 28 or Sprint 30 tunes anything.**

## The call this needs (NR-334)

Ben ruled on 2026-08-18 (ruling 8 of NR-331) that the docs were wrong and the **code** was right — keep 400. That ruling was taken against the *production* number, before this divergence was known. The second half is still open: does the **harness** follow production down to 400/one-band, or does **production** follow the struct default up to 4000/six-band? The struct's own comment attributes the six-band ladder to Ben, 2026-08-12, so this is not a stale default — it is a second live intent.

## The work, once the call is made

1. One shared helper that builds the production `history_sim_params`, called by `make_hard_coded_world` **and** by every harness — so the two cannot drift again.
2. Re-run Sprint 27's B384 group on the production config and re-state its findings against it.
3. If both configurations are deliberately kept, every Era −1 harness row must **name which config it measures** in its own output line.

items.title: Every world has exactly 31 population centres, and two thirds of nations contain none
items.summary: Measured 2026-08-18 by the new substrate_census harness (BL-462's sibling, Sprint B1). Population centres are clamp(grid_tiles/1000, 20, 40) at population_generation.cpp:147 — pure grid AREA, no seed term and no nation term. The grid is fixed at 312x145, so the expression evaluates to 31 on every world ever generated. Across three seeds with land areas of 10,745-16,074 tiles and 43-67 nations, the count was 31, 31, 31. 109 of 169 nations across the sweep (64%) contain no population centre at all.
items.design:
## What the census measured

| seed | land tiles | nations | settlements | buildings | built % | settled % | land within 3 tiles of anything |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 12,724 | 43 | **31** | 94 | 0.74% | 0.24% | 27.6% |
| 1 | 16,074 | 67 | **31** | 71 | 0.44% | 0.19% | 22.5% |
| 2 | 10,745 | 59 | **31** | 150 | 1.40% | 0.29% | 31.3% |

**Roughly 70% of walkable ground is more than three tiles from any building, settlement or road.** That is the most direct available reading of Ben's *"much land that is untamed"* (2026-08-18), and it is now a number rather than an impression.

Seed 0 detail: 26 of 43 nations have **no road network**, 38 of 43 have **no market**, and road tier 3 (Highway) is never generated anywhere.

## The defect

`src/world/population_generation.cpp:147` — `clamp(grid_width * grid_height / 1000, 20, 40)`.

The grid is a fixed 312x145 = 45,240, so this is `clamp(45, 20, 40)` = **40** before other passes trim it to 31. It reads **grid area**, which is constant, rather than **land area** or **nation count**, both of which vary by 1.5x across seeds. No world can be more settled than any other.

The clamp bounds were set for the 180x84 grid and never revisited when the 3x map landed with the 0 CE refocus (2026-08-12).

## Why priority A

It is the single largest contributor to the world not reading as civilised, and it is upstream of three other complaints: a nation with no settlement gets **no road network** (`road_generation.cpp` returns early below two centres), **no market**, and therefore no visible hub. So one constant explains the settlement gap, the road gap and the hub gap at once.

## Direction, not a chosen number

Derive the target from **land area and nation count** rather than grid area, then **pin the bands by measurement** across seeds — never by picking a figure here. Ben's standing preference is honest constraints over clamping, and BL-224's discipline is report-then-tune. The census harness added by Sprint B1 is the instrument; re-run it across a wider sweep before and after.

**Assertion owed:** the census's F1 row — *every nation holds at least one population centre* — was written, measured, and **fails at 64%**. It is deliberately non-gating today. It becomes the acceptance test for this item.

items.title: Logistic Points - a throughput currency the transport network generates and both goods and force spend
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-18: "Let's begin codifying Logistic Points in this sprint. It's an important layer for military and goods transport." The concept does not exist anywhere in Io today - no doc, no code, no prior item. This item opens it as DESIGN work inside Lane C1 rather than a build, because its shape has four materially different readings and picking one silently would be the expensive mistake. RULED 2026-08-20 (NR-343): LP is a per-tick RATE - a regenerated throughput allowance, used or wasted each tick, never banked; only the goods it moved carry over. The earlier settled prose recording LP as a stock is superseded by this dated ruling.
items.design:
## What this overturns, stated rather than hidden

`docs/economy/SUPPLY.md` § Infrastructure gates lists **per-node throughput capacity** as *out of prototype scope*, and Sprint 25's block re-affirmed it in its own exclusion list (NR-312). Ben's 2026-08-18 instruction overturns that. Under DELIVERY.md's newest-dated-wins rule this is legitimate; it is recorded here so the reversal is traceable and SUPPLY.md is corrected as part of landing the work, not before it.

## Why the shape is right, independent of the details

**BL-325 ruling 3: one reach field — economic reach IS military reach.** Logistic Points make that ruling *quantitative* rather than merely topological. Today the network answers "can this be reached"; LP would let it answer "how much can move, and what else does that displace". That is the same single network serving goods and force, which is the ruling exactly.

It also gives four already-shipped systems a consumer they lack: road tiers currently only discount cost (`1/(1+0.5*tier)`), ports have no throughput meaning, the Reach lens shows a binary field, and convoys queue without contention.

## The trap this item exists to avoid

**`military_points` was deleted on 2026-08-17 (BL-455) for being a write-only accumulator**, and NR-257 deleted five resources for the same reason a day earlier. A Logistic Point that is generated and never spent — or spent and never felt — is the identical defect with a new name.

**Non-negotiable: LP lands with its consumer in the same batch.** No accrual-only first cut.

## The four readings, which are NOT interchangeable

| | Reading | Generated by | Spent by | Grain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | **Per-node capacity** | a node's tier/size | convoys passing through it | node |
| b | **Per-nation budget pool** | the nation's infrastructure | every movement inside it | nation |
| c | **Per-corp allowance** | the corp's own assets | that corp's convoys and units | corp |
| d | **Shadow-Empire style** | infrastructure, as a stock | supply *and* unit upkeep, with distance as the multiplier | mixed |

(d) is the reference Ben's other generation steers point at (PLANETOLOGY.md models the planet pass on Shadow Empire explicitly), and it is the reading in which LP most directly couples military to goods — which is the stated reason for wanting it. It is also the largest.

**Open, and owed to Ben before any code:** which reading; whether LP is a *stock* that accumulates or a *rate* refreshed each tick; whether an over-subscribed network fails, queues, or degrades; and whether the player sees LP as a number, a lens, or only as a refusal.

## Determinism

Whatever the reading, allocation under contention must be **order-independent** — a deterministic priority rule over a sorted set, never first-come by iteration order. `world::state_hash` and the convoy determinism check (`convoy_command.cpp` R5) are the guards.

## Sequencing note

Filed `requires: BL-448` (stance) only because it is promoted inside Lane C1 and shares that sprint's design attention — **not** a code dependency. If interdiction (BL-458) later reads LP, that coupling is filed there, not here.

---

## SETTLED 2026-08-18 (Ben): reading (d) — the Shadow Empire model

*"I'm thinking we can lean heavily on the shadow empire system, and change things if a strong need arrives."*

That closes the four-way fork above. LP is a **stock** generated by infrastructure and spent by both goods movement and unit supply, with **distance as the multiplier** — the reading in which military and economic transport draw on one pool, which is the whole reason Ben asked for it.

**"Change things if a strong need arrives"** is the licence, and it is narrower than it sounds: adapt where Io lacks a Shadow Empire prerequisite, not where the mechanic is merely inconvenient. Every substitution gets written down with the reason, so a later reader can tell an adaptation from a drift.

**The naming rule still binds.** Shadow Empire is a *mechanism* reference exactly as Rome is in HISTORY.md — no term, label or proper noun crosses into Io. "Logistic Points" is Ben's own phrasing and is fine; nothing else transfers by default.

**What this does NOT settle**, and is owed before code: what generates LP and at what rate, the exact consumer that lands in the same batch, the order-independent allocation rule under contention, whether LP enters `world::state_hash` (convoys deliberately do not), and the smallest honest first cut.

---

## CORRECTION 2026-08-18: LP is a RATE, not a stock

The ruling above records LP as *"a **stock** generated by infrastructure"*. **That is wrong about Shadow Empire, and the correction is fidelity to Ben's instruction rather than a departure from it.**

In Shadow Empire, LP is a **per-turn throughput allowance**. Capacity is regenerated each turn by the network and is then used or wasted; what carries over is the resource *stock* it moved, never the points. LP is the pipe; the tanks are separate.

Three consequences, all in Io's favour:

- A rate **crosses no tick boundary**, so it needs no `state_hash` entry and no serialisation — and Io has no save/load layer to add one to.
- A stock that accumulates while never binding is the `military_points` failure with extra steps.
- It removes the largest open question about where LP lives between ticks, because it does not live between ticks.

**Caveat, flagged rather than buried:** this claim comes from Shadow Empire guides, not from anything in this repo. It is the one load-bearing assertion here with no `file:line`, and Ben should confirm it before it hardens.

**CONFIRMED 2026-08-20 (Ben, NR-343 resolved):** LP is a per-tick RATE - regenerated throughput, used or wasted, never banked; the goods it moved are what carry over. The caveat above is discharged; the rate reading is settled.

## Io already owns Shadow Empire's OTHER half, twice over

SE runs **two** currencies: LP (*how much*) from nodes, and Logistical AP (*how far*) from links, where infrastructure quality buys **distance, never capacity**.

Io has the AP half already. `road_traversal_multiplier` = `1/(1+0.5*tier)` is AP-per-hex under another name (`logistics.cpp:62-66`), and `body_reach_field` is SE's free-AP envelope expressed as a cost field.

**So adopt SE's node half and refuse its link half.** Importing AP would be a second parallel distance budget, which BL-325 ruling 3 (one reach field) forbids outright.

## LP is a CAP, not a price

Io's convoy **already charges distance, in credits** — `unit_cost * dist * qty * (1 - node_discount)` (`supply_system.cpp:371`) — and Shadow Empire charges no money for haulage at all.

Adding LP as a second *price* would double-charge distance and move every economy golden. **Credits stay the price; LP decides whether the leg is admissible at all.**

## THE FIRST CUT AS DRAFTED IS REJECTED — two adversarial passes, both structural

Recorded so the next attempt does not re-run into them:

1. **The inertness proof is unachievable as sequenced.** Two-pass allocation reorders float subtractions on a hashed field (`corp.balance -= leg.cost`, `supply_system.cpp:399`), so a "rate-zero, byte-identical" commit cannot pass *at any rate*. The proof pattern BL-409 and BL-454 used does not transfer here, and pretending it does is how a golden gets blessed dishonestly.
2. **LP as drafted has no spatial locus.** § 1 justifies it as *"how much can move through HERE"* — a node — then pools generation per `(corp, body)`. That is not throughput; it is a per-corp haul allowance, which is the exact abstraction `military_points` was deleted for.
3. **The LP cost formula is never specified**, yet the allocation sort key is a function of it. If cost is proportional to distance, LP *is* haulage cost again; if flat, the sort degenerates to tiebreaks.
4. **The base allowance would be the whole mechanic.** No corp is seeded an `inland_logistics_hub`, so *"your own nodes decide how much you may move"* is fictional at the shipped generator — nearly every corp would sit at exactly the base allowance.
5. **The AI pays LP and cannot build the generator.** `corp_ai.cpp` has no `port` and no `inland_logistics_hub` build candidate, so the rate would be an asymmetric tax on rivals.
6. **A reserved military share deletes the coupling it exists to create.** Two budgets means guns and butter stop competing, which was the whole point.
7. **`supply_decay_permille` would ship a one-way ratchet** — `supply_recovery_permille` is *also* 0.0, so a unit short for one tick is permanently degraded.

**What survives and should lead the next attempt:** LP as a cap rather than a price; the node half only; the rate reading; two consumers (`commit_convoy` and `run_unit_upkeep`) that both already exist; and the finding that goods-vs-force priority is currently decided **invisibly by tick phase order** — convoys claim before armies on every code path, so "the army goes unsupplied" is an inherited default nobody chose.

items.title: A building 40 tiles from its market clears at the same price as one on the market tile
items.summary: Found 2026-08-18 by the research pass that was sent to evaluate Ben's same-province discount. The discount was rejected as a duplicate of convoy haulage cost - but the pass found the REAL hole it was reaching for. Ordinary auto-surplus clearing debits the corp pool and credits income at ref_price with no convoy created and no leg priced (market_clearing.cpp:747-760). So distance INSIDE a market catchment costs nothing at all: a site on the market centre tile and one forty tiles away clear identically.
items.design:
## The defect

`market_clearing.cpp:747-760` — the auto-surplus path debits the corp's pool and credits income at `ref_price`. **No convoy is created and no leg is priced.** Distance within a catchment is therefore free.

That is the honest version of *"locality is not priced"*. Ben reached for it with a same-province discount; this is the same instinct aimed at the actual hole.

## Why it matters beyond realism

It silently flattens every siting decision inside a catchment. A remote deposit and a deposit on the market's doorstep are worth the same, so the map's geography stops paying — which undercuts the placement-suitability surface, the Opportunity lens, and BL-436's (processing underearns extraction) whole margin question.

## Why it needs NO new grouping

This is the finding that killed the province-discount framing. `price_convoy_leg` **already computes exactly this leg**, over the same reach field BL-325 ruling 3 makes canonical. Nothing new has to be invented, partitioned or named.

## Where to charge it

**At the accrual site, never inside `resolve_price`.** The precedent is BL-343's extraction levy: charge where the flow is *accounted*, not where the price is *resolved*, so the market's quote stays one honest number and the order book's total order is untouched.

Charging inside `resolve_price` would make price depend on who is asking, turning one number into a per-pair matrix and breaking the determinism hash with it.

## Open, and owed to Ben

Full leg cost, or a fraction? Full cost makes remote extraction abruptly unprofitable everywhere at once.

**Measure first.** This makes every remote site less profitable simultaneously, and it lands on an economy whose value-add step is already inverted (BL-436) and whose benchmark reads bankrupt. Sequence it *after* BL-443 (debt floor) so the measurement is readable.

items.title: The province becomes real - a seeded 3-5 tile partition of the land, with the battle footprint as its first consumer
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-19 from Ben's battle-surface elicitation ruling: a battle's footprint is the PROVINCE ENVELOPE, so the province (the 3-5 tile locality cell named in the 2026-08-18 spatial vocabulary, designed-not-built) gains its first confirmed consumer. Its founding purpose - the same-province locality discount - was REJECTED by NR-342's research pass, so without this consumer the object had none. SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, elicitation): blocks with terrain-seam jitter; single-tile coastal fragments merge into their lowest-id neighbour. The algorithm is designed - see the 2026-08-19 block.
items.design:
## Why now

The spatial vocabulary (settled 2026-08-18) defines the province as a small, uniform, purely
spatial cell of ~3-5 tiles between tile and region - and GLOSSARY.md records it designed, not
built: no province type, no tile->province mapping. The one job it was named for (pricing
locality before the market) was rejected the same day (NR-342: it duplicates convoy haulage
cost). BL-467 (battle state in the world) now needs it as the engagement envelope, which is a
real consumer rather than a speculative one.

## Shape

- A deterministic, seeded partition of each body's LAND tiles into contiguous cells of ~3-5
  tiles. Every land tile in exactly one province. Ocean excluded - water is a movement mode
  (the terrain functions' own ruling), and a sea battle is not this item.
- Purely spatial and uniform, deliberately NOT the region: no name, no owner, no culture, no
  serialised state. Derived at generation and recomputable - nothing crosses a save seam
  (there is no save layer).
- Owed before build: the algorithm. Two candidates - (a) seeded anchor scatter + bounded BFS
  fill (the region machinery's shape at a smaller grain), (b) regular tiling deformed at
  coasts. Whichever wins must be pure, seeded, and order-independent.

## Constraints

- **The partition enters battle identity.** BL-467 folds the province id into the battle's
  seed stream, so a partition change re-rolls every battle in a world. The partition is part
  of world generation and versions with it; it is never patchable in place.
- **Not a price mechanism.** NR-342's rejection of the same-province discount stands; this
  item must not smuggle a locality price back in. If Logistic Points (BL-464, the throughput
  layer) later wants the province as its node grain, that coupling is filed there.

## Consumers, in order

1. BL-467 (battle state) - the engagement envelope and the battle map frame. Confirmed.
2. BL-464 (Logistic Points) - candidate node grain, named by NR-342. Not settled.

## SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, elicitation) - the algorithm

Ben's two rulings: **blocks with terrain-seam jitter** (over uniform blocks and anchor
scatter), and **single-tile coastal fragments merge into their lowest-id neighbour**.

Three passes, the whole partition a pure function of (world seed, grid, land mask, terrain).
No RNG stream is consumed - every draw is a stateless fold from the seed, the campaign_battle
identity idiom, so the partition can never perturb another system's draws.

### Pass 1 - base blocks

Per body: an origin offset (dx, dy in {0,1}^2) folded from (world seed, body id), then 2x2
offset-coordinate blocks over land tiles. Interior blocks are size 4 - inside the 3-5 band.
A 2x2 offset block is hex-connected on the odd-r grid. Base province id derives from block
coordinates - stable, allocation-free.

### Pass 2 - terrain-seam jitter

One deterministic sweep over block-boundary tile pairs (a in P, b in Q, hex-adjacent),
visited in ascending tile id, each tile moving at most once. A swap score folds from
(seed, tile ids) and is WEIGHTED BY SEAM EVIDENCE: a river edge or a landform/composition
change between a and b raises the preference that the border sit ON that seam - borders
drift onto rivers and terrain edges, which is the whole point of the ruling (a province
edge on defensible ground makes the battle envelope's boundary mean something).

A tile crosses the border only if: both provinces stay within size 3-5, both stay
hex-connected (the mover may not be a cut vertex of its source), and neither has already
been resized this sweep beyond the clamp. Single pass, fixed order, no cascade.

### Pass 3 - coastal repair

(a) **Strait split**: a province whose land tiles are not hex-connected (a 2x2 block
bisected by ocean) splits into connected components, sub-ids assigned smallest-tile-id
first. No province ever spans water. (b) **Fragment merge** (Ben's ruling): a ONE-tile
province merges into its lowest-id hex-adjacent province on the same landmass; a true
islet with no neighbour stands alone. Post-merge coastal sizes may exceed 5 - coasts bend
the band, recorded rather than hidden. The jitter clamp never creates a 1-tile province,
so every merge here comes from coastline intersection, not from pass 2.

### Data, lookup, identity

A stored per-body tile->province map (u32), built at generation, recomputed never
serialised (nothing to save; no save layer). Province ids are stable derivations of
(base block id, component index), so sorted-id iteration gives BL-467's battle discovery
its deterministic order, and battle identity folds (body, province id).

### Verification - province_partition harness (verifier-headless)

Asserts: every land tile in exactly one province; no ocean member; every province
hex-connected; interior sizes 3-5 and coastal sizes 1-5+merge; recompute identity (the
replay guard); the stored map agreeing with a fresh derivation; and - positively - that
jitter moved at least one border onto a river or landform seam on the reference world, so
the pass cannot silently no-op. The world_determinism suite gains a provinces-on case when
the partition wires in.

### Delegated to promotion (NR-348)

The seam-evidence weights (river vs landform vs composition edge), the swap-score
threshold, the exact offset fold, and which tile fields carry river evidence - named at
promotion against the real tile model, not guessed here.

items.title: A battle becomes a thing in the world - the province engagement envelope, the stepped span, and the withdraw verb
items.summary: SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, battle-surface elicitation): footprint = the PROVINCE ENVELOPE with units keeping tile positions; terrain = ONE pair for the whole battle; pacing = SEVERAL ROUNDS PER TICK. Takes over the uncalled-resolver strand of BL-315 (armed house conflict spine): the engagement trigger and world-held battle state that MILITARY.md lists absent. resolve_campaign_battle finally gets its production caller.
items.design:
## The three rulings this item is built on (Ben, 2026-08-19, elicitation form)

1. **Footprint: the province envelope, units keep tiles.** Hostile units standing in the same
   province are drawn into one battle; the province frames the fight. Units never abstract
   into a pool.
2. **Terrain: one pair for the whole battle**, exactly as resolve_battle already takes it.
   Per-unit terrain was offered and declined.
3. **Pacing: several rounds per tick** - a shorter, but still real, withdrawal window.

## Reconciliation with the 2026-08-13 tile-token ruling - extension, not overturn

BL-315's ruling 2 (units as tokens on the tile map, "not armies at province grain") stands
untouched: command grain stays the tile - units move tile to tile and stand on one. What the
province adds is the ENGAGEMENT grain: which standing tokens are in the same fight, and what
map the battle draws. The two grains answer different questions and both rulings are Ben's,
five days apart, and compatible.

## What it takes over

MILITARY.md § What is absent attributes the engagement trigger and battle state to BL-315
(armed house conflict spine). This item now owns both; BL-315 keeps the resolver, the
force-command model and the single-sourced roster. The bridge (unit_to_stack_entry, BL-459)
already exists with only a harness caller - this item gives it the production caller.

## The engagement trigger

After stance (BL-448) lands: a battle OPENS when units of two corps stand in the same
province and at least one holds a hostile stance toward the other. Directed hostility
suffices - the ambush property BL-448 paid two tables for: the declarer attacks, the target
is drawn in regardless. Discovery each tick walks provinces in sorted (province id, corp-pair)
order, so battle creation is order-independent. A corp pair fights at most one battle per
province at a time.

## The state
