A world-held record: {province, attacker, defender, participating unit ids, rounds_fought,
per-round trace}. The trace is retained for the span (dispatches BL-468 and the card BL-469
read it) and discarded at battle end - nothing crosses a tick boundary except the record
itself. Seed identity: fold the PROVINCE id where campaign_battle_identity folds tile_index
today - same splitmix64 shape, role order preserved (a role swap stays a different stream).

**Determinism harness first, in-memory replay only** - the BL-448 precedent verbatim: no
serialiser exists, so assert on replay, never a save round-trip.

## Pacing and the window

rounds_per_tick is AUTHORED DATA in campaign_battle_params (the corp_ai_params precedent),
not code. At the shipped max_rounds 6 and a first-cut rounds_per_tick 3, a full battle spans
2 ticks and the player gets one real between-tick decision. Tuning the window is a data edit.

## The terrain pair - SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, review-verdict form; was the filed proposal)

The envelope spans 3-5 tiles and the battle reads one pair. Proposal: the pair comes from the
DEFENDER-side tile with the highest terrain_defence inside the envelope - the defender is
presumed to anchor on the best ground, which is what defending means, and terrain_defence
already multiplies the defender only. Deterministic: max over sorted tile ids. Ben may prefer
the anchor tile of the first-engaged unit, or the province's dominant terrain.

## Per-unit hits

resolve_battle returns per-side loss fractions; the map needs per-unit hits. Each side's
round loss is distributed across its participating units deterministically: proportional to
count, remainder assigned by ascending entity id. No new draws - a pure function of the
round outcome. Supply and quality already enter through unit_to_stack_entry, so an
unsupplied unit is weaker and its losses bite harder, with no second mechanism.

## The withdraw verb

corp_verb::withdraw_from_battle {province}. Legal for either participant; applies at the tick
boundary before the next round batch; price is the existing three-term withdrawal cost (base
+ per-round + pursuit), which the card surfaces live. A rejection mutates nothing. The
ACTIONS.json dictionary entry lands with the verb - the stale-entry rule. The rival scorer
may call it under the standing scored-utility exception; scoring it well is future work, not
this item.

## Aftermath

Losses land on unit counts per round batch (a battle weakens units while it runs). Field
held by the side that stayed, defender on ties - both resolver rules already. Zero-count
units are disbanded by the upkeep pass's existing cleanup, which runs last in the economy
step.

items.title: The battle speaks - deterministic round dispatches in the comms dock
items.summary: SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, battle-surface elicitation): the battle surface is the Selection card PLUS comms dispatches - no dedicated ledger. Each round batch appends dispatch lines to the comms dock: deterministic text, a pure function of the round trace, phrased as the company's field officer reporting. The design-research finding this encodes: commanders in every era experienced battle as dispatches, so the comms dock is the historically honest channel - and it is native to the corporate-console fiction.
items.design:
## Shape

Each stepped tick, every live battle (BL-467) appends one dispatch per round batch to the
comms dock. Text is a PURE FUNCTION of the retained round trace - no extra draws, so the
dispatch layer can never move the sim. Phrase selection folds from the battle identity plus
round index, through seeded template banks (the BL-290 tongue-bank precedent): sci-fi
voice, never Earth-flavoured, per the naming rule.

## The phase vocabulary - presentation only

Rounds are mechanically uniform; the dispatches ladder them: opening rounds speak as
skirmish, the middle as commitment, a large swing as crisis, an approach to the rout
threshold as wavering, withdrawal as breaking off WITH ITS PRICE NAMED, and the aftermath
names who holds the field and what it cost. The same vocabulary keys the battle card's phase
readout (BL-469), so the two surfaces never disagree.

## The channel - SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, review-verdict form): the standing Field channel

A standing **Field** channel beside Public (chat_state's channel model takes this in one
row; the player is an implicit member). Reason: battle traffic must not drown the market
chatter the Public channel carries, and a channel can be muted. The alternative - posting
into Public - costs nothing but mixes voices. Ben's call.

## Question-log entry (BL-260, required)

"What is happening in my battle, and is it time to leave?" - the dispatch stream is the
answer surface; the card (BL-469) is the command surface. Enforcement is authorship, not
machinery.

items.title: The battle card - the province map in the Selection band, each unit hit by hit, and the priced exit
items.summary: SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, battle-surface elicitation): the battle is watched and commanded from a new Selection-band card kind. Centrepiece: the province's 3-5 hexes drawn large, each participating unit a marker on its own tile, hits landing per round, with the withdraw price live while the window is open. Ben's framing verbatim: "sketch a map of each unit being hit."
items.design:
## Selection model

A new Selection kind: **battle**. Clicking any tile inside an active battle's envelope - or
the battle's canvas marker - selects the battle first; the click-cycle extends to
battle -> unit -> building -> tile. Deselection rules unchanged (SELECTION.md owns them).

## The card

- **The map**: the province's hexes drawn large - the tile card's hex-neighbourhood widget
  is the pattern to reuse. Each participating unit a marker on its own tile (positions are
  real; the envelope ruling kept them). Per-round hits render as decaying flashes plus a
  loss pip per unit, read from BL-467's retained trace.
- **Per-unit strength bars** with the existing derivation read: count x quality x supply -
  the unit card already prints it; the battle card keeps the decomposition so an unsupplied
  unit visibly fights weaker.
- **Readouts**: round / max, the phase word (shared vocabulary with BL-468, so card and
  dispatches never disagree), both sides' aggregate strength.
- **The withdraw press**: shows the CURRENT price with all three terms legible (base +
  per-round + pursuit) updating as rounds pass - the one decision the span contains, made
  visible while the window is open. Confirm on press (the declare_hostile confirm pattern,
  BL-449). Disabled with a reason when the battle is not the player's.

## Canvas marker

A battle-in-progress glyph over the envelope (ICONS.md discipline: shape, meaning, usage,
colour source catalogued; identity colours stay in presentation.hpp). The deleted unit
chevron (BL-294) is the cautionary precedent - this marker earns its place as the alert that
pulls the eye to a fight, which a battle with no glyph cannot do.

## Visibility

The player's own battles show everything. A rival-vs-rival battle shows under the
competitor-visibility rule (BL-068): the marker, the participants, the outcome - internals
private, no per-unit detail.

## Verify driver rider (NR-345)

No headless binding can select a unit - or a battle. The work adds verify.select_battle (or
extends the select cycle) so the card is photographable; without it every visual requirement
on this item is green-but-blind, which is the exact failure NR-345 records.

## Question-log entries (BL-260, required)

The card: "How is my battle going, and what does leaving cost right now?" The marker:
"Where is fighting happening?"

items.title: Units learn to walk - march, halt and disband as corp verbs, path-marching across ticks on the one distance metric
items.summary: SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, unit-verb elicitation): movement is a PATH MARCH across ticks paying the one distance metric; the seam EXTENDS corp_verb (one seam, one dictionary family, one rejection enum); first cut is MARCH + HALT + DISBAND. Unpins the unit from its muster tile - the gap BL-393 (units write-only) documented and deliberately deferred. Carries two riders: the blackboard export of units (BL-393's open half) and a deliberate, recorded goods-vs-armies claim order (NR-344). [COMPLETE 2026-08-19: march_unit/halt_unit/disband_unit extend corp_verb (corp_command.{hpp,cpp}); movement_order {dest,path,next_index,progress} on unit_component (components.hpp); run_unit_march resolves per-class march_points_per_class (economy.lua, recipe_registry) against tile_traversal_cost (promoted out of logistics.cpp) with fractional carry-over, ascending-entity-id, in the slot BL-467s battle-discovery phase will occupy. Rider 1 (blackboard units export) and Rider 2/NR-344 (war flips the queue, corp_is_mobilised) both landed. state_hash extended to cover movement_order. tools/verify/unit_march_harness.cpp: 53/53 PASS (legality+snapshot-mutates-nothing, resolution+carry-over+arrival, halt/disband, NR-344, state-hash replay determinism, blocked-path recompute determinism). Regression-checked: stance_determinism 36/36, unit_upkeep 62/62, logistics_harness all PASS, full ProjectIo build clean. MILITARY.md updated (new Marching section, Build status, What is absent).]
items.design:
## The three rulings this item is built on (Ben, 2026-08-19, elicitation form)

1. **Path march.** A unit walks tile-by-tile across ticks toward a destination, paying the
   SAME traversal costs everything else pays (road_traversal_multiplier, the reach metric).
   Instant hop and step-per-press were offered and declined.
2. **One seam.** march/halt/disband are corp_verb rows with a unit-id argument - no parallel
   unit_command enum. BL-314's "future unit_command seam" phrasing resolves to THIS: the
   seam corp_command.hpp already is, extended. One dictionary family, one rejection enum.
3. **First cut: march + halt + disband.** Merge/split, garrison and scout stay out; the
   formation item (BL-472) owns group behaviour.

## Why path march is the load-bearing choice

It makes BL-325 ruling 3 kinetic: roads genuinely project force, because a marching column
moves at the speed of its ground. A column crossing provinces can be MET - which is what
gives BL-467's engagement trigger honest work - and a unit can now walk beyond the reach
envelope, which is what makes the (currently disabled) out-of-supply decay reachable in play.

## The verbs

- **march_unit {unit, dest tile}.** Sets a movement order on the unit. Rejections:
  unit not the actor's (rejected_not_owner), unit or tile nonexistent / dest is ocean
  (rejected_invalid), unit currently in a battle (rejected_state - withdraw first, BL-467's
  verb). A rejection mutates nothing - the seam is an untrusted input boundary.
- **halt_unit {unit}.** Clears the order. Halting an unordered unit is rejected_state.
- **disband_unit {unit}.** Erases the unit. No refund - manpower walks away. Confirm lives
  in the UI (BL-471), never in the seam.

## Movement resolution - deterministic by construction

- A movement order stores {dest, path, progress}. The path is computed ONCE at order time -
  cheapest route under the same cost function body_reach_field uses, ties broken by ascending
  tile id - and recomputed only when invalidated (a blocked step). No per-tick Dijkstra.
- **march_points per tick is AUTHORED DATA** (economy.lua § military, the campaign_battle_params
  precedent), spent against per-tile traversal cost with fractional carry-over. One speed for
  all units in the first cut; per-class speed (a wing outpacing a line) is BL-472's ground,
  and any speed stat derives from the roster row - the NR-322 one-source discipline.
- The pass visits marching units in ascending entity id (the upkeep pass's rule, same reason),
  after battle discovery: a unit that marched into a hostile province this tick fights before
  it can march out next tick.

## Rider 1 - the blackboard export (takes over BL-393's open half)

export_corp_blackboard gains a units section: id, tile, type, count, derived strength, order
state (marching to / holding / in battle). A corp reading its OWN force engages no visibility
rule; rival units stay under BL-068's competitor rule. Without this the rival scorer would
command blind, and BL-314's dictionary entries could not state an expected_output honestly.

## Rider 2 - the claim order is decided on purpose (NR-344)

Goods currently beat armies to the supply network by tick phase order alone. FIRST-CUT
PROPOSAL, recorded not settled: keep convoys-before-armies as the DECLARED default - trade
is the base identity and force is the expensive exception - but state it in MILITARY.md and
economy_system.cpp's phase comment, so when Logistic Points (BL-464) makes the two contend
for one pool, the priority is a written rule, not an accident. NR-344 stays open for Ben.

## Downstream

- The rival scorer gets march as a candidate under the standing scored-utility exception -
  legality here, scoring quality is conflict-AI work (BL-450's arc), not this item.
- ACTIONS.json entries are transcribed AFTER the seam lands - BL-314 (unit verb family) owns
  the transcription and now requires this item.
- The determinism guard: state-hash replay with marching units, plus a harness case where a
  re-run recomputes an invalidated path identically.

## SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, review-verdict form) - two calls move

- **March speed is PER-CLASS, now.** The one-speed first cut is overturned. Speed keys on
  the roster row's cls - an authored per-class table in economy.lua § military (numbers are
  data; the class comes from the one roster source, the NR-322 discipline). A composite unit
  (BL-472) moves at its slowest component's class speed - the slowest-member rule applied
  inside the token.
- **The claim order: WAR FLIPS THE QUEUE (resolves NR-344).** At peace, convoys claim the
  supply network first - trade is the base identity. A corp that is party to any declared
  hostility row (either direction - being attacked mobilises too) feeds its units first that
  tick. Evaluated per corp at tick start from the stance table (BL-448), so the priority is
  deterministic and readable, and mobilisation has a visible logistical cost the moment war
  is declared.

items.title: The army becomes visible and commandable - the unit canvas marker, the march target mode, and the unit card presses
items.summary: SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, unit-verb elicitation): the unit marker rides with the verbs - marching invisible armies is absurd. Replaces the chevron deleted uncalled in BL-294 with a marker that has earned its place: units now do something. Adds the march target mode, the unit card's March / Halt / Disband presses, and the headless drivers NR-345 demands.
items.design:
## The marker

A unit glyph at the unit's tile (ICONS.md discipline: shape, meaning, usage, colour source
catalogued; identity colours from presentation.hpp). A marching unit shows its heading; a
unit in battle defers to the battle marker (BL-469). BL-294's deletion is the standard to
clear: that chevron drew nothing anyone could act on. This one marks an object with verbs.

## The command surface

- The unit card (Strength / Roster pages exist) gains an Orders page: current order state
  (holding / marching-to with remaining cost / in battle), and the March, Halt, Disband
  presses. Disband confirms (the BL-449 declare_hostile pattern); Halt is plain; March
  enters target mode.
- **March target mode**: the place-road/place-building targeting pattern - click a
  destination tile, escape cancels. The projected path and its tick cost preview on the
  canvas before the click commits, so distance is priced BEFORE the order, not discovered
  after. Toggle rule applies: re-pressing March while armed disarms it.
- The hover card adds the order state line.

## Verify drivers (the NR-345 debt, paid here)

verify.select_unit(id-or-tile) and verify.march_unit(unit, col, row) land with the surface,
so the card, the marker and the target mode are all photographable headless. Without them
every visual requirement on this item is green-but-blind.

## Question-log entries (BL-260, required)

The marker: "Where are my forces, and where are they going?" The Orders page: "What is this
unit doing, and what can I tell it to do?"

items.title: Formations - composite units that march and fight as one, with preset templates keeping the rock-paper-scissors legible
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-19 from Ben's elicitation note: "a structure to manage groups of units that work as one team over a series of regions... beforehand we should just use common groups, such as 1000 infantry split by groups of 200. And 100 tanks + 400 infantry." A formation is a named grouping of units that marches as one and fights as one side, carrying a doctrine row - which finally gives doctrine_row its campaign consumer. Preset templates first, player-authored composition deferred. The template wheel preserves the class matrix's rock-paper-scissors at formation grain.
items.design:
## What a formation is

A world-held grouping: {members: unit ids, template, name}. Members keep their own
unit_component rows - count, type, supply, tile - so nothing about the settled unit model
moves. The formation adds three behaviours:

1. **Marches as one.** One movement order for the group; the formation moves at its slowest
   member's speed (the historical truth - a column is its baggage). Members co-tile with the
   formation's anchor tile in the first cut; spreading members over adjacent tiles is a
   follow-on, not this item.
2. **Fights as one.** In BL-467's envelope, a formation is one side's stack: members'
   unit_to_stack_entry rows plus the TEMPLATE'S doctrine_row. This is the design's quiet
   win: doctrine_row (frontal_bonus, flank_fragility, mountain_penalty, siege_stance) ships
   today as pure data with no campaign consumer - the formation template is that consumer.
3. **Is commanded as one.** form_up {units, template} / disband_formation {formation} as
   corp_verbs on the one seam (the BL-470 ruling). march_unit accepts a formation id where
   it accepts a unit id.

## Ben's examples, read against the model (2026-08-19 note, verbatim anchors)

"1000 infantry split by groups of 200" - a template speaks RATIOS over classes and a
sub-group granularity, not absolute headcounts (hire_batch_manpower is 50 today; the batch
size is data and may move). "100 tanks + 400 infantry" - a 1:4 shock-to-foot combined-arms
mix; in class terms the tank IS the cavalry class's industrial row, so the template is
era-invariant: the same mix is lancers-and-levies at 0 CE and armour-and-rifles at 1960.
Era-invariance of templates matches BL-314's verbs-are-era-invariant ruling exactly.

## The template wheel - keeping rock-paper-scissors legible

The class matrix already runs infantry > ranged > cavalry > infantry. Templates COMPOSE it
rather than replace it, and the wheel must survive at formation grain:

| Template | Mix (by weight) | Doctrine lean | Beats | Loses to | Ground |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Line** | 80 infantry / 20 ranged | frontal_bonus high, flank_fragility high | Screen | Wing | anchored, rough - defence country |
| **Screen** | 60 ranged / 40 infantry | low frontal, low fragility | Wing | Line | forest, highland - cover country |
| **Wing** | 60 cavalry / 20 infantry / 20 ranged | high frontal, mountain_penalty high | Line | Screen | plains - open country |
| **Spearhead** | 20 cavalry / 60 infantry / 20 ranged | moderate everything, low fragility | none hard | none hard | any - the generalist premium |
| **Train** | 30 siege / 50 infantry / 20 ranged | invest stance | (fortifications, future) | everything in the open | roads - it barely moves |

- **Line > Screen > Wing > Line** is the wheel, and it derives from the matrix: a Line's
  infantry mass closes on a Screen's ranged core; a Screen's massed ranged shreds a Wing's
  cavalry; a Wing flanks a Line's fragility. No template beats its counter through raw
  numbers alone at even strength - that is the legibility invariant, and the harness asserts
  it the way combat_harness R3 already asserts doctrine purity.
- **Spearhead is deliberately counter-free both ways** - the combined-arms generalist
  (hammer-and-anvil, armour-plus-infantry). Its edge is flexibility, priced by never having
  a favourable matchup. Ben's tanks+infantry example lands here.
- **Train exists for the future fortification system**; in the open field it is prey, which
  the matrix already encodes (siege uniformly weak). Its escort keeps it from being a free
  kill, no more.
- **Terrain rotates the wheel, it never breaks it**: mountain and forest amplify Line and
  Screen (terrain_defence, doctrine mountain_penalty against the Wing), plains amplify the
  Wing, wetland punishes Wing and Train (attrition 350, the marsh-stops-armies reading).
  All of that is EXISTING numbers - templates add no new terrain table.

## Presets first, customisation deferred - explicitly

The five templates ship as AUTHORED DATA (lua, the params precedent): ratios, sub-group
granularity, doctrine values. Player-authored templates (choose your own mix and doctrine)
are a named follow-on slice, not silently dropped - the note's "this can be customizable"
is the licence, and the deferral is so the wheel is proven legible before it is player-bent.

## Determinism and naming

- form_up validates every member (owned, same tile, not in battle) and mutates nothing on
  rejection. Formation ids are entity ids; iteration follows the sorted-id rule everywhere.
- "Formation" enters GLOSSARY.md with the work (the name-it-first rule). Template display
  names are authored data and must come from the seeded banks if they are ever generated -
  never Earth proper nouns. Line/Screen/Wing/Spearhead/Train above are design labels, not
  shipped strings.

## Open, named

- Per-class march speed (a Wing should outpace a Line) - interacts with slowest-member rule;
  derive any speed from the roster row (NR-322's one-source discipline).
- Whether a formation's members can straddle tiles (frontage on the battle map) - deferred
  with the spreading follow-on.
- Reinforcement: can a unit join a formation mid-campaign at distance, or only co-tile?
  First cut: co-tile only.

## 2026-08-19 - the presets are COMPOSITE UNITS; formations remain above them (Ben's correction)

Ben, review-verdict form: *"I was imagining formation pre-sets as composite units rather
than formations. My bad with the word choice. We can use both though."* So the model gains
a layer and keeps the other - two objects, both real:

- **Composite unit** - ONE unit entity whose composition spans classes: a composition
  vector over {cls -> manpower share}, set by its template at muster. "Muster a Spearhead"
  is a single press at the base: 100 shock + 400 foot arrive as one token, one marker, one
  order, one supply read. The FIVE PRESET TEMPLATES SHIP AT THIS GRAIN (all five confirmed
  this date). unit_to_stack_entry becomes one-to-many - one stack entry per component
  class - and derived strength sums components. The hire gate is the union of every
  component row's gates; the price sums component costs through the existing power-mod
  pricing. It marches at its slowest component's class speed.
- **Formation** - the grouping of units (simple or composite) that marches and fights as
  one, as designed above. This is where customisation and the multi-unit army live -
  "1000 infantry split by groups of 200" is a formation of five infantry units. Doctrine:
  a lone composite unit fights under its own template's doctrine row; a formation's
  template doctrine governs the whole side when grouped.

The wheel analysis is unchanged - it holds at whichever grain instantiates it, because both
resolve to the same class-mix stacks.

items.title: Clicking a tile shows its province - the Selection band renders the locality cell, and the tile preview outlines it
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-19 (review-verdict form): "let's add an item here about rendering provinces with a selection band when a user clicks on a tile. This should also be rendered in the selection tile preview." The province (BL-466, the 3-5 tile locality cell) becomes visible the moment a tile is selected - before any battle exists to draw it.
items.design:
## Shape

- The tile card gains a province read: the selected tile's province, shown as its member
  tiles. Provinces are deliberately nameless (purely spatial, the GLOSSARY ruling), so the
  read is structural - "one of 4 tiles" plus the outline - not a name line.
- **The hex-neighbourhood preview outlines the province**: the member tiles of the selected
  tile's province get a distinct stroke inside the existing preview widget. One visual
  vocabulary with the battle card (BL-469 draws the same cell as the engagement envelope),
  so the player has already met the shape before the first battle draws it.

## Question-log entry (BL-260, required)

"Which tiles move and fight as one locality with this one?" - the answer surface a player
needs BEFORE committing units, since the envelope decides who is drawn into a fight.

items.title: A Diplomatic lens shows stance geographically, replacing the all-corporations table as BL-449s surface
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-19: the all-corporations Stance table (BL-449) is too much information at once and not the shape he pictures for this. Redirect: a Diplomatic overlay_mode joining the corporation/country/resource/etc. roster, tinting tiles or corp markers by the players stance toward the owning corp (Hostile/Friend/Neutral/Unknown per NR-350), so relationships read on the map the way ownership and production already do. Supersedes the table-column approach BL-449 shipped and NR-353 found unreachable - that column is retired, not fixed. [PARKED 2026-08-19 (Ben): basic military function (each corp starts with an army) takes priority; diplomacy surfacing is a tangent for now. In-flight WIP (not landed, not verified) sits uncommitted-to-main on branch worktree-agent-a2b81665b3439a110, commit 6ad58a3 - resume from there rather than restarting.]
items.design:
## Why this instead of the table

BL-449 tried to put four extra facts (Reach/Capital/Share/Stance) plus three presses into the all-corporations table already living in the narrow shell fold-out column. NR-353 found the result unreachable in play - the Stance columns buttons render off the panel edge, and BL-111 had already narrowed that same table once before for the identical reason (six columns collapsed to single-glyph headers).

Ben's redirect, 2026-08-19: this is backend-useful information, not player-facing information in that shape. A lens is the existing vocabulary for at-a-glance relational state across many entities at once - Corporation lens already tints tiles by owner, Country lens by nation. Diplomatic stance is the same shape of fact (a per-corp category) and belongs in the same family, not in a giant table.

## Scope (design-owed - settle before promoting)

- Where the tint reads: tile fill (like Corporation lens) vs. a marker/ring on each rivals HQ/buildings (lighter-weight, avoids implying stance is a REGION when it is a relationship between two corps). Lean toward the marker/ring approach given stance is corp-to-corp, not corp-to-territory - but this is the first open question for Ben.
- Colour/glyph vocabulary for Hostile/Friend/Neutral/Unknown - four states need four legible marks, and Unknown (BL-068 gated, NR-350) must read as distinct from Neutral rather than simply absent.
- Bar or off-bar placement (LENSES.md "Bar" column) - stance is not yet consequential (BL-448 lands the substrate inert), so off-bar (like Scarcity/Industry/Reach) may be the honest placement until BL-315/BL-467 give it a gameplay payoff, matching how those lenses graduated onto the bar only once their consequence landed.
- Whether the three transition presses (Declare Hostile / Offer Friendship / Return to Neutral) live in the lens itself (a marker click opens a small popup) or move entirely into the Selection panel (see BL-475) - if the latter, this lens is READ-ONLY and simpler to design.

## What it does not carry

No new data model - BL-448s stance.hpp tables are already correct and load-bearing. This item is purely the map-surface read; BL-475 is the per-corp detail + action surface.

## SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, elicitation form)

- **Tint target: TILE FILL, not the marker/ring recommendation.** A deliberate overrule — Ben wants stance to read as a territory tint like the Corporation lens, not a per-building marker. This makes the corp-vs-territory framing in this item's earlier text moot; the lens colours the rival's owned tiles by the player's stance toward them, same visual family as Corporation/Country.
- **Bar placement: ON THE BAR, not off-bar.** A second deliberate overrule of the "not consequential yet" reasoning — Diplomatic joins Corporation/Country/Resource/etc. as a primary, always-reachable lens from day one rather than waiting for BL-315/BL-467 to give stance a gameplay payoff.
- **Marker click: clicking a tinted tile/rival selects that corp and jumps to its Selection panel** (BL-475) — the lens is a read surface, selection is the existing canvas click-to-select path, no bespoke popup.
- **Presses live ONLY in the Selection panel (BL-475)** — confirmed, matches the recommendation. This lens carries no interactive presses of its own.
- **Colour vocabulary: the recommended scheme, confirmed.** Hostile red, Friend green, Neutral grey, Unknown a dashed/hollow grey ring — Unknown must never read as a blank tile (NR-350).

Both overrules recorded per this project's standing practice of flagging where Ben's choice differs from the filed recommendation and why it matters: tile fill reads Diplomatic as territory-like from the start, and bar placement means it ships visible before it has any gameplay consequence — a deliberate legibility-first call, not an oversight.

items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-19, companion to BL-474: expand the per-corporation Selection ledger to carry stance and any other relevant from-our-perspective detail, replacing the all-corporations tables Stance column as the place the three transition presses (Declare Hostile / Offer Friendship / Return to Neutral) actually live. Selecting a rival corp (from the canvas, a lens marker, or the corporations list) shows the relationship as ONE corps detail, not a row in a giant comparison table. [PARKED 2026-08-19 (Ben): basic military function (each corp starts with an army) takes priority; diplomacy surfacing is a tangent for now. In-flight WIP (not landed, not verified) sits uncommitted-to-main on branch worktree-agent-a2b81665b3439a110, commit 6ad58a3 - resume from there rather than restarting.]
items.design:
## Why the Selection panel, not the table

SELECTION.md already owns the pattern for one-entity detail across the game (Active/Focus/Selection states, shared per-entity content builders the Tile Ledger and hover card also use). Stance-toward-one-corp is exactly that shape of fact - it belongs where a player already looks to learn about ONE thing, not crammed into a table meant to compare MANY things at once (which is what made BL-449s column unreachable, NR-353).

## Scope (design-owed - settle before promoting)

- Where in the Selection cards existing layout the stance block sits, relative to whatever a corp selection already shows (BL-081/BL-214s roll-up cards, per question_log.jsons corporation_dashboard entry).
- The three presses (Declare Hostile with its confirm popup on the demolish precedent, Offer/Accept Friendship, Return to Neutral) move here from the retired table column - same corp_command verbs from BL-448, same rejection handling, same NR-350 visibility gate (do not show anything for an undiscovered corp beyond Unknown).
- Whether BL-474s lens markers are clickable to select-and-jump here, or selection only happens via the existing canvas/list paths - affects whether BL-474 needs any interactivity of its own.

## What it does not carry

No new data model or verbs - BL-448s stance.hpp and its four corp_command verbs are unchanged. This is purely re-hosting an already-correct interaction onto the right surface. ACTIONS.json/question_log.json entries move with it (retitle rather than duplicate - BL-449s existing corporation_panel entries describe the retired surface).

## SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, elicitation form, alongside BL-474)

- **This item now owns ALL three transition presses exclusively** — BL-474's lens is confirmed read-only, so Declare Hostile / Offer Friendship / Return to Neutral live here and nowhere else.
- **Entry point confirmed: selecting a tinted tile/rival under the Diplomatic lens (BL-474) jumps here** — the existing canvas click-to-select path, no new selection mechanism needed.
- Layout position within the existing Selection card stack is still an implementation call for whoever promotes this — not re-elicited, low-stakes relative to the placement/interaction questions above.

items.title: Every corporation starts with an army, not just the player
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-19: park the diplomatic lens tangent, basic military function first - at the very least, each corporation must start with an army. `corporation_generation.cpp:1507` seeds a `military_base` + one unit for the PLAYER ONLY ("Rival corps get no such seeding", BL-330/BL-331). Extend the same seeding to every named rival (not BL-365 background filler firms, per Ben's scoping call) so the military layer is symmetric from turn one instead of a player-only opener. [COMPLETE 2026-08-19: extracted the player-only block into `seed_starting_military(world&, entity_id)` (anonymous namespace, corporation_generation.cpp), called once for the player FIRST (byte-identical tile pick vs pre-BL-476) then once per generated rival in stable corp_ids order - never for a BL-365 background firm, since generate_background_firms runs in a separate later pass. New harness tools/verify/rival_military_seeding_harness.cpp: 8/8 non-background corps seeded (1 military_base + 1 unit each) in the canonical world, determinism confirmed across two generations, land-poor-nation graceful skip confirmed via a synthetic all-ocean-tile world - 17/17 PASS. corp_terrain_matrix and military_capability_harness re-run clean; determinism_harness 25/25 PASS. docs/military/MILITARY.md corrected (Build status + writers list).]
items.design:
## What exists today

`corporation_generation.cpp` (~line 1506-1617) seeds the PLAYER corp, and only the player corp, with one `military_base` building near its HQ (or the nearest valid land tile) and one `unit_component` (roster index 0, 50 manpower, `supply_factor_permille = 1000`). The comment there is explicit: *"Rival corps get no such seeding; this is a player-experience opener, not a generation-wide asset."* Rivals can only ever acquire military opportunistically, later, through `corp_ai.cpp`'s scored `hire_unit` candidate (BL-324) - and that candidate presumably scores near-zero early game since a rival with no military_base has nowhere to hire FROM.

## Scope, settled 2026-08-19 (Ben, asked directly given the cost/balance fork)

**Player + named rivals, NOT BL-365 background firms.** A background firm (`corporation_component::is_background`) exists purely to fill a body's production/demand gap and is not meant to read as a competitor - arming it is out of scope here and would be a separate, larger balance call (especially once upkeep rates move off zero, BL-454).

## The fix

The player-only block is a single inline scope, not a function - lift its body into a shared helper (e.g. `seed_starting_military(world&, entity_id corp_id)`) taking the corp id, keeping the exact same logic (nearest valid land tile to HQ, one military_base, one 50-manpower unit at roster index 0). Call it once for the player (unchanged behaviour) and once per generated rival corp (`is_player == false && is_background == false`) in the same corp-generation pass, so the seeding stays deterministic and generation-time rather than becoming a first-tick economy action.

**Graceful-empty stays graceful-empty.** The existing skip-if-no-valid-land-tile behaviour (a land-poor nation just does not get seeded, no crash) applies per-corp exactly as it does today for the player.

**No change to `corp_ai.cpp`'s ongoing hire_unit scoring** - this is only the generation-time seed, not a change to how rivals grow their military afterward.

## Requirement (item-spanning, headless)

Assert every non-background corp (player + rivals) ends generation owning exactly one `military_base` and one `unit_component`, deterministic across two same-seed runs, and that a background firm owns neither. A land-poor nation with no valid tile is exempted, matching the existing graceful-empty case - assert this does not crash rather than asserting every corp always gets seeded.

items.title: Each era has a collapse state to avoid — that is what defines meta
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-19 (version-alignment form, verbatim): "We should have a paradigm that makes nuclear war unlikely, but a clear looming threat for this Era. In general, each era has a 'collapse' state to avoid - and that's what defines meta." The paradigm: every era names ONE collapse state — the ancient era's is imperial collapse (the Fall arc, Sprint 30's strain machinery); the industrial/space era's is the nuclear rupture (BL-333's parked arc, HISTORY.md stage 6). Meta systems (tech BL-479, law BL-480, policy BL-155/BL-156) must couple their levers to the era's collapse pressure — a tech or law is interesting because it moves the world toward or away from the brink, not because it moves a growth curve.
items.design:
## The paradigm

Each era carries one named collapse state the world can fall into, and the meta layer — tech, law, policy — is defined by its relationship to that state. Design-owed: (1) name the ancient era's collapse pressure in ERAS.md terms and wire it to the Fall arc's strain/hegemony machinery (Sprint 30) so campaign-era play inherits a live, legible threat, not lore; (2) specify how the modifier vocabulary (BL-479) expresses collapse-coupled effects — e.g. a law that trades treasury for cohesion, a tech that extends reach at the cost of strain; (3) the nuclear paradigm for the space arc stays parked with BL-333 but this item's framing must not contradict it. RULED (Ben, 2026-08-20): **genuinely reachable.** The collapse state is a real campaign fail-state, not a pressure valve the meta always buys off. Two consequences bind the design: (1) the strain/collapse machinery Lane A builds for the Era −1 sim (Sprint 30) is a SHARED mechanism the campaign inherits, not generation-only plumbing; (2) meta levers (tech BL-479, law BL-480) can move the world toward or away from the brink but must never be able to wall it off entirely — a world played badly enough collapses, and the meta is interesting because the threat is real.

items.title: Research becomes a currency the corp spends
items.summary: Extracted from parked BL-087 (Era-1 tech/quest system) piece 2 on Ben's 2026-08-19 verdict — the accrual/cost/debit mechanism Sprint D2 needs. Fall-arc ruling 6: science is SPENT, not reached. What shipped 2026-08-17 (BL-455) is a LEVEL — condition_subject::science as a threshold; spending needs a debit the level model never had: an accrual (exists), a cost per ladder node, a debit at the moment a node is taken. Loads docs/research/ancient_tech_ladder.json (92 objects) and authors the T1-T2 gates with ENFORCED prerequisites. The condition_set.hpp:70-75 comment block asserting reached-not-spent must be rewritten in the same change (verdict M2) — it is true today and becomes a lie the day this opens.
items.design: Design-owed. Boundary settled 2026-08-19 (verdict M3, Ben's pick): this is the live arc's spend mechanism, extracted from BL-087 piece 2; BL-087's era-event/quest framing stays parked. Sprint D2 is the build home; sequence after BL-479 (the effect union) so a purchased node can express more than a building unlock.

items.title: A tech can express a buff — the effect union and the modifier vocabulary
items.summary: Sprint D1's build item (Lane D, opened 2026-08-19). The whole tech effect vocabulary today is one field — tech_gate's unlocks_structure (audit finding 5: a 9:1 condition-to-effect asymmetry). Widen it to a closed tagged union {unlock_structure, modify_scalar}, and author the closed modifier-subject vocabulary — every scalar a tech OR A LAW may move — shared between tech and law, which is the reason tech and law are one lane. [COMPLETE 2026-08-19: merged 455b3f9 (branch commit 8c62fe1). Union {unlock_structure, modify_scalar} + shared modifier_set.hpp vocabulary (incl. collapse_strain for BL-477); applied per-corp at earn time; 35/35 new harness, tech_gate 33/33 unmodified, no-effect world bit-identical vs a genuine pre-change build. corp_modifiers derived/unhashed — BL-107 carries the recompute-on-load debt (NR-371).]
items.design:
## Shape

1. `tech_effect` becomes a closed tagged union: `unlock_structure` (existing behaviour, unchanged) + `modify_scalar {modifier_subject, op (+/-/×), magnitude}`. No open-ended callback, no Lua hook — a closed vocabulary keeps it deterministic, serialisable and legible.
2. `modifier_subject` is a new closed enum in `src/world/modifier_set.hpp`, authored once and shared by tech (this item) and law (BL-480): the scalars a meta effect may move (e.g. extraction_rate, processing_yield, unit_upkeep, logistics_cost, wage_floor). Append-only once serialised; ONE appender per batch (the Fall-arc collision rule, which assigns the append to Lane D).
3. Application seam: effects apply PER-CORPORATION at the economy tick's existing read sites — research is not a world fact (v0.1.4 done-definition). An empty effect list is a no-op; a world where no tech carries modify_scalar is bit-identical to today.
4. Serialisation window: no save format exists (BL-107 open), so the stored-field change is compile-time today and a migration later — the same cheap window BL-344 used.
5. Collapse coupling (BL-477): the vocabulary should be able to name at least one strain/cohesion-adjacent subject so era-collapse meta is expressible, even if no tech uses it yet.

Guards: harness proves (a) a granted modify_scalar tech moves the named scalar for the earning corp only, (b) rivals' scalars unchanged, (c) no-effect worlds bit-identical (state_hash), (d) union round-trips through the recipe/tech registries without touching the ImGui viewer (BL-310's radial viewer reads names only).

items.title: A law has an author, and a tax is a transfer
items.summary: Sprint D3's build item (Lane D, opened 2026-08-19 in one batch with D1 per Ben's verdict). Three defects, one item: struct law has no author (BL-155: non-deferrable — "a law with no author is not migratable later"); the enacted levy DESTROYS money (debited from the corp, credited to nothing); and enactment is a debug checkbox on the player's balance ledger — a corporation flipping world law. [LANDED 2026-08-19 @ merge c00bba8, awaiting two things: Ben's live look at the read-only levy line (R3 half) and the NR-382 rate ruling — the placeholder 1.0/unit all-resources rate, biting now the law ships enacted, drives every rival insolvent; ai_skill bands left red-and-attributed, deliberately unblessed. Conservation/scope/repeal all green (14/14 + 24/24).]
items.design:
## Shape

1. `struct law` gains `enacting_nation` (entity id) and an applicability scope (the enacting nation's jurisdiction — corps whose taxed flow lands in its territory). A law with no author cannot exist any more.
2. `nation_component` gains a `treasury` (credits). The levy becomes a TRANSFER: debit the payer, credit the enacting nation's treasury, sum conserved — asserted by harness.
3. Enactment moves off the player's ledger. The balance-ledger checkbox (balance_ledger.cpp:277-279) is removed; the seeded law set is enacted at generation by its author nation, deterministically. A nation CHOOSING to enact mid-campaign is the BL-202/BL-203-shaped scored decision the 2026-08-18 nation grant permits — may stub as generation-seeded only this sprint, with the seam shaped for the scorer.
4. The player's laws surface (BL-186, amended today) reads: which laws bind me, whose, what they cost me — browse-only.
5. Wages-above-a-legal-floor: severable; take only if the modifier vocabulary (BL-479) lands first and names wage_floor, else leave to a follow-on.

Guards: harness proves (a) conservation (levy sum debited == treasury sum credited), (b) scope (an out-of-jurisdiction corp pays nothing), (c) repeal returns bit-identical to baseline, (d) no player-reachable enact control remains (the untrusted-boundary rule applies if any seam verb is added — reject, never clamp).

items.title: The blackboard export is 60x too large for a local model — fuse the triples, hoist the envelope
items.summary: BL-335's measurement (2026-08-19): one player blackboard read is ~74 KB / ~18.5K tokens, refreshed every decision because state changes each tick — an 8B local model at 8K context cannot hold ONE export, and at 32K it eats half the window per decision. 96% of the bulk is two families: the market price/demand/supply triple (351 facts, 53%) and the rival-building owner/tile/type triple (258 facts, 43%), each fact repeating a ~70-byte constant envelope (_v, t, confidence, provenance) around ~45 bytes of payload. The word-interface direction (AI_OPPONENT.md § 10, tight-local-model bias) requires the compact encoding this item builds.
items.design:
## Shape

1. FUSE the per-subject triples: one row per (market, resource) carrying price+demand+supply; one row per rival building carrying owner+tile+type. Pure re-encoding, zero information loss — measured to cut the bulk ~3x (to ~25 KB / ~6K tokens); a tabular encoding lands ~12 KB / ~3K tokens.
2. HOIST the constant envelope (_v, t, confidence, provenance) to a stream header; facts carry payload only, with per-fact overrides where a value genuinely differs.
3. FILTER seam (client-side or a query arg): own-assets slice (~3 KB) + market rows for resources the corp holds or can extract. The full export stays available — the compact form is an additional shape, not a replacement, so BL-204's goldens and every existing consumer are untouched.
4. Guard: a harness asserts the fused form round-trips to the same fact set as the verbose form on the canonical world (information-preservation, not golden bytes).

Consumers: BL-306 (client loop) reads it; BL-279's corpus (parked) inherits it for free. Version: v0.1.16 (The watch) — it gates a usable local-model session on the seam BL-412 is landing.

items.title: The Economy panel pools view leaks every corp's stockpiles to a played session
items.summary: Found in passing by the BL-408 god-view build (2026-08-19): economy_panel.cpp draw_pools lists EVERY corp's (corp, body) pool quantities to an ordinary played session — a straight violation of the BL-068 competitor-visibility rule (rival buildings visible, internals private), predating the god-view work entirely. God view now makes this information legitimately visible under spectate; the played-session path must redact rival pools to the same standard the Selection/hover surfaces already meet.
items.design: Gate draw_pools rows on ownership: the player's own pools render as today; rival rows redact quantities (or drop) unless spectating && god_view. Follow the exact test BL-408 planted at its read-sites so the two paths cannot drift. One file, one gate; verify with a played-session capture beside the existing spectator_god_view.lua ON/OFF legs.

items.title: Transformation (E4): the mandate resets the regime, the map holds
items.summary: The dynastic-cycle allegory's exit: strain > cohesion WITH high works/institutions resolves by re-founding, not fragmentation - same borders, new polity, reset strain, partial capacity regression, legitimist creed. The cheapest culmination (no map change) and the one that keeps region counts stable.
items.design: Exit selection is DETERMINED by the state vector at break (COLLAPSE.md open question 2's lean): the works/cohesion-infrastructure level is the discriminant between E4 and E1. The successor keeps the ancestor's name lineage via the phoneme generator's variation path, not a fresh mint.

items.title: Exodus (E5): the rump state and the migration
items.summary: A breaking or absorbed polity with an open frontier survives displaced - Settle fired as a survival verb. Yields a small, high-cohesion survivor far from home with maximal grudge, and frontier regions gaining unearned population/capacity. The map texture Sprint 29 wants: capitals in strange places, with reasons.
items.design: Trigger: E1/E3 resolution where a frontier region within reach is unheld. The chosen-remnant creed locks legitimist + max grudge (COLLAPSE.md pattern library).

items.title: The Slow Fade (E6): senescence below a relevance threshold
items.summary: No rupture: a major chronically NEAR the break, never over it, erodes - piecemeal border recession and a demotion below the hegemony measure. The Metropole's default ending and the sim's best source of interesting small nations at 0 CE: proud creed, high grudges, disproportionate reach.
items.design: Detection: N consecutive years in the top strain band without a break event. Effect: periphery provinces detach singly (to neighbours or owner_none) at a deterministic trickle; the polity survives as a minor.

items.title: Cohesion reads interdependence: the substrate for systemic collapse (E7)
items.summary: The Bronze-Age allegory: one break cascades because neighbours' cohesion rested on the broken polity's trade and tribute. Needs cohesion to carry an interdependence input - a real design decision, deliberately sequenced AFTER E1-E4 land and are measured (COLLAPSE.md's own caution).
items.design: A per-polity term derived from routes/works shared with neighbours; an E1/E3 event that severs them debits the survivors' cohesion. Candidate for a RARE outcome band asserted by sweep, never scripted. The most expensive culmination; hold until the others are measured.

items.title: Seeded polity creeds from the pattern library, biasing the culmination
items.summary: COLLAPSE.md's ideological axis made mechanical: creed is seeded data per polity (mandate / remnant / stewardship / restoration leans from the pattern library), and the state vector that determines the exit includes it - same strain, different story, different ending, deterministically.
items.design: A small enum-weighted axis set written at polity creation and mutated only by culminations. Consumed by: exit determination (E4 vs E1 vs E5), Release scoring (stewardship-lean raises it), and Sprint 29's nation-character payload. This is where 'the story IS the character payload' becomes code.

items.title: The six-strategy roster as seeded weighting profiles over polity verbs
items.summary: Tortoise / Pulse / Hydra / Phoenix / Metropole / Temple as data: per-polity verb-weighting profiles assigned at seed, deterministic, replayable. The tuned-attractors ruling means these are the diversity source the sweep asserts distinctness over - not templates that script outcomes.
items.design: Each profile is a weight vector over {Campaign, Settle, Invest, Consolidate, Release} plus thresholds (Pulse's strain switch, Hydra's release band, Phoenix's neighbour-collapse gate). Profiles live in history params so tuning is a data change. Distinctness asserted by BL-490.

items.title: History-tab narration per culmination and narrative pattern - quiet by design
items.summary: Each culmination emits its narrated line(s) in the history log, minted from the pattern library (the declinist mirror precedes the break; the mandate withdrawn explains E4; the garden given away recasts E2). Ruling 2026-08-20: surfaces in the history tab only - seeing beats telling, deep-dig optional, never chrome pushed at the player.
items.design: Template lines keyed by (culmination, creed) filled with phoneme-generated names. Driven, not narrated: every line is emitted BY an event that occurred. Sibling to BL-300 (myth/theology), which owns the authored bank's voice; a devolution that plays back as silence looks like a bug (COLLAPSE.md open question 4).

items.title: The attractor sweep: four allegory arcs at reported rates, strategies distinct
items.summary: The tuned-attractors ruling's enforcement: across N seeds, assert each allegory arc (fragmentation, devolution, transformation, cascade) occurs at a stated, REPORTED rate - never clamped - and each strategy profile is observably distinct in lifespan, fragment count and successor share. Two indistinguishable strategies mean one is dead weight; a culmination that never fires is scope to cut.
items.design: Extends the existing sweep harness. Rates pinned BEFORE tuning (the adversarial pass's discipline: the number must not be chosen to match the result). The strategy x culmination matrix in COLLAPSE.md is the literal assertion table.

items.title: Event-driven quiet provinces: stable interiors wake on events, not per year
items.summary: Perf rung 2 of COLLAPSE.md's 4000-year ladder. Most of 4000 years, most provinces do nothing; give stable interior provinces a fast path that wakes on border change, strain band crossing, or route loss - never a per-year evaluation.
items.design: Wake conditions are pure functions of sim state (deterministic; asserted by the prehistory-on determinism case). Converts per-year cost from O(provinces) toward O(changes). Depends on BL-320's spatial index + incremental aggregates landing first (rung 1).

items.title: Deterministic banded year grain: quiet ages step coarse, crises step yearly
items.summary: Perf rung 3. Simulate quiet bands at 5-10 year steps with scaled verb effects; drop to yearly grain when any polity's strain, war state, or culmination proximity crosses a band. Targets the year count directly - the rung that makes 4000 years affordable.
items.design: The grain switch MUST be a pure function of sim state - seeded, replayable, asserted by the determinism case - or it is a die roll wearing a timestep (COLLAPSE.md's own words). Verb effect scaling at coarse grain must be exact-integer so no drift separates a watched run from a skipped one.

items.title: Record the run on change, at the reader's grain
items.summary: Perf rung 4 - the recording half, which BL-425 measured as the real hang (>8 min Debug for the per-year time-lapse). Snapshot ownership on owner_changes (already exists) plus per-decade otherwise; narrated lines are events, not per-year state. The history tab scrubs decades in practice.
items.design: Memoise the record at generation time in BL-427's world-snapshot cache so --verify pays nothing. Un-parks scripts/verify/parked/history_ages.lua as part of landing (BL-425's own close-out).

items.title: Extend the Era -1 run to the 4000-year ladder and re-pin the bands
items.summary: The ruling itself (Ben, 2026-08-20): the 400-year band was a placeholder; the aim is 4000 years so the four allegory arcs chain sequentially per world. Extends prehistory_years and the band ladder; re-pins every generation golden and the BL-224 non-hegemony bands by measurement.
items.design: Lands LAST in the perf ladder - after BL-320 (rung 1), BL-491 (rung 2), BL-492 (rung 3), BL-493 (rung 4) - and only if the /O2 measurement fits the generation budget; the honest fallback (2-3 completed arcs per world, all four attractors asserted across the sweep) degrades density, never determinism. Reverses the Sprint 26b doc-truth correction knowingly: HISTORY.md's 400-year note gains a dated supersession pointing here.

items.title: Held convoy cargo stays visible to the price signal
items.summary: Ben's ruling on NR-317 (2026-08-20): a held convoy's cargo counts in the scarcity/price calculation, aligning with BL-422's convention for held sell orders (held stock stays visible so scarcity is not gameable). Closes the parked-outside-the-economy exploit shape without new cost machinery - one convention everywhere.
items.design: Wherever resolve_price / the rarity input aggregates available stock, include cargo aboard held convoys at the destination market's scope, exactly as BL-422 includes held orders. No upkeep charge, no expiry - the hold stays a legitimate strategic pause; only its invisibility goes. Assert with a headless case: holding a convoy moves no price.

items.title: Ordnance upkeep rate leaves zero when battle consumption lands
items.summary: Ben's ruling on NR-321 (2026-08-20): the ordnance (and food_rations) upkeep rates ride Lane C's engagement trigger - the first real draw coincides with combat that spends it, one golden re-bless instead of two. Until then rate 0.0 is a deliberate, dated state, not an oversight; this item is the tripwire so it is not forgotten.
items.design: When the engagement trigger lands: pick small nonzero rates, run the BL-454 checks (N units debit exactly N x rate, empty pool decays at the authored scalar), measure how far rival balances move, re-bless the economy goldens. Makes BL-457's admission argument (ordnance has a consumer) true at runtime, which chain_depth's exemption currently asserts only structurally.

items.title: Delegate the corpus: saved agent roles and directory-scoped instruction files
items.summary: Ben's ask (2026-08-20): the corpus (~650K tokens) is too large for one session to consume, so sessions should be prompted differently by role. Saves the recurring worktree sub-agent roles as .claude/agents/ definitions (economy-dev, ui-dev, generation-dev - joining code-reviewer) and adds directory-scoped CLAUDE.md files for src/world and src/ui, each a pointer set into the authority docs plus the always-on invariants for that layer.
items.design: Three principles, all pointer-not-copy: (1) a role definition carries its reading list, invariants and commit discipline so a spawn needs only the task brief; (2) a directory CLAUDE.md loads automatically and carries only what every session in that directory needs - the root CLAUDE.md stays the router; (3) prose never duplicates an authority doc, it cites one, so drift cannot fork the design. Deliberately NOT done: thinning the root router (larger, separate call) and a doc-steward role (bookkeeping stays in the main session per DELIVERY.md). Landed same-session; DELIVERY.md § Sub-agents gained the pointer paragraph.

items.title: One shared axis-to-candidates resource table behind the hire gate and the hire debit
items.summary: Code-review audit finding (2026-08-20): debit_hire_cost (corp_command.cpp:92-105) hand-mirrors unit_roster.cpp:143-154's campaign_gate_input preference lists, guarded only by a comment saying they must match. The BL-394 free-hire bug class recurs the day one side gains ordnance (BL-454/BL-457 work) and the other does not.
items.design: Lift the three axis preference lists into one table in unit_roster.hpp; both the gate and the debit consume it. Land BEFORE the military-milestone roster work touches either site. Assert with the existing hire harness: gate pass implies a matching debit for every axis.

items.title: Harness round-trips every corp_verb through the wire parser
items.summary: Code-review audit finding (2026-08-20): a new verb touches four surfaces (enum, apply_corp_command, corp_ai scorer, ACTIONS.json) and the pattern has already failed three times (main.cpp:391-401 - BL-324/BL-293/BL-350 each left verbs unreachable over the wire). Nothing machine-checks parser coverage; the AI-opponent milestone multiplies external callers.
items.design: Headless harness: enumerate corp_verb, serialise each through the wire encoding, parse back, assert a non-default verb and no silent degradation. Wire it into the standard verifier-headless set so a grown enum fails the same day.

items.title: Determinism harness widens from seed 0 to a real seed sweep
items.summary: Code-review audit finding (2026-08-20): determinism_harness.cpp:12-17 still says world-gen is not seedable and checks only the zero-seed world - but the seed IS threaded now (hard_coded_world.hpp:27-33). Nonzero-seed determinism, exactly what the Era -1 extension (BL-494) and nation behaviour lean on, has no guard.
items.design: Sweep a small fixed seed set (e.g. 5 seeds), assert byte-identical regeneration per seed and distinct state hashes across seeds. Update the stale header comment. Land before further history-sim work.

items.title: Lenses become a descriptor table instead of three inlined regions of the planetary canvas
items.summary: Code-review audit finding (2026-08-20): body_surface_canvas.cpp (2,906 lines) inlines the lens system across three non-adjacent regions - 12 draw_*_key functions (136-760), per-lens precompute (1162-1409), per-tile colour chain (1655-1736). Every new lens is a 3-4-touchpoint edit; nothing ties a lens's key legend to its colour rule, so they can drift invisibly.
items.design: Mechanical move, not redesign: a lens descriptor {key-draw fn, tile-colour fn, optional precompute} in a new lenses.cpp; the canvas iterates the table. Behaviour-identical - verify with the existing lens goldens at 0.0000%. Pays back on the next lens the roadmap adds.

items.title: Selection panel's ten private glyphs move into the icons catalogue
items.summary: Code-review audit finding (2026-08-20): ten glyph_* functions (selection_panel.cpp:985-1102) follow the (dl, centre, r, colour) contract but live outside icons.{hpp,cpp}, invisible to the catalogue - glyph_swap already exists twice in the same file. Violates the standing glyph invariant in src/ui/CLAUDE.md.
items.design: Move the ten into ui::icons, dedupe glyph_swap, catalogue each in ICONS.md per its recipe. Behaviour-identical; verify with the selection-panel goldens.

items.title: Selection panel, hover card and tile ledger converge on the shared per-entity builders
items.summary: Code-review audit finding (2026-08-20): SELECTION.md claims the Tile Ledger and hover card share the per-entity content builders, but entity_summary.cpp has effectively one consumer - selection_panel, hover_content and tile_inspector each build their own rendering of the same facts, three drifting paths. The cost triples when military/political entity kinds arrive.
items.design: Convergence onto the existing seam (entity_summary / selection_card), not new architecture: per entity kind, one builder both surfaces call, surface-specific framing kept at the call site. Verify with the selection and hover goldens; note any legitimate rendering differences in SELECTION.md as they surface.

items.title: A stateful strain accumulator: digestion retires strain, loss does not
items.summary: Sprint 30's NEW-6, filed. Replace the stateless burden (burden=(held-40)x4, recomputed from current holdings) with an accumulating pressure that can break. The adversarial pass's shape assertion is the acceptance test: the strain term must NOT decrease when holdings decrease - losing provinces must never make an empire logistically stronger.
items.design: Design in COLLAPSE.md section 'What the sim must grow' item 1 and the Pulse strategy: strain accumulates with expansion tempo and breadth-over-knee; Consolidate years retire it at an authored rate; province LOSS retires nothing (the grievance stays). Deterministic scalar per polity, serialised alongside cohesion_q. The Pulse strategy only exists once this lands - alternating Campaign/Consolidate must be arithmetically better than continuous Campaign at equal holdings.

items.title: The collapse itself: fragmentation into named successor polities
items.summary: Sprint 30's NEW-7, filed. When strain exceeds cohesion unmanaged, the polity fragments into successor polities along province/culture seams, emitting owner_none where nothing coheres and a real eliminated-polity event where alive=false is currently silent. COLLAPSE.md culmination E1.
items.design: Successors route through the seeded phoneme generator - struct polity has no name field today and the naming rule is absolute (no placeholder). Each successor inherits a restoration-lean creed and a grudge toward whichever neighbour fed on the break (Sprint 29's payload). Break lines are a deterministic function of province adjacency + culture + local cohesion, never a roll.

items.title: Promote the hegemony measure from the sweep harness into the engine
items.summary: Sprint 30's NEW-8, filed. The sweep harness has a reporting threshold; the engine has nothing that can name, gate or narrate a great power. Promote it so polity::major means something and culminations/narration can key on it.
items.design: One function over holdings share + reach; the same number the sweep already computes, computed once and stored per polity per year. Consumers: the strain accumulator (BL-504, majors accumulate), the attractor sweep (BL-490), the history-tab narration (BL-489).

items.title: A Release verb: voluntary devolution into client polities
items.summary: The Hydra strategy's verb and culmination E2 (devolution - the managed release, the British-empire mechanism). A fifth scored polity verb: shed peripheral provinces into a client successor BEFORE strain chooses the break line. Second, voluntary trigger on BL-505's fragmentation machinery.
items.design: Scored like the other verbs (ruling: verb, not threshold rule - keeps it inside the nation-behaviour grant's shape). Value rises with strain and falls with cohesion headroom. The asymmetry is the point: released clients carry LOW grudge toward the core (devolution buys goodwill fragmentation never does); the core's creed shifts imperial->mercantile and keeps its reach.

items.title: Strained majors are readable prey: weakness as an observable, not telepathy
items.summary: Culmination E3 (absorption) needs rivals to score Campaign against a high-strain target - but no polity may read another's internal scalar. Expose weakness through observables: lost battles, stalled campaigns, supply shortfalls - the same tells the player sees.
items.design: A small derived 'apparent weakness' value per polity computed from public events only (battle outcomes, campaign stalls), consumed by rivals' Campaign scoring. Keeps the no-telepathy discipline STRATEGIES.md set at corp grain.

items.title: Conquering a strained polity imports its strain - absorption is never free
items.summary: COLLAPSE.md E3: without transfer, eating a strained major is a free lunch and absorption becomes the dominant exit. The conqueror inherits holdings AND a share of the victim's accumulated strain.
items.design: On province transfer from a polity above a strain band, a proportional strain quantum moves with it. One subtraction and one addition on BL-504's scalar; the absorbed culture persists as grudge+creed inside the new borders.

items.title: Reach feeds a second, slower strain inflow - the Metropole also breaks
items.summary: NR-356's hole: a reach-hegemon with few holdings never trips a holdings-fed accumulator, dodging Sprint 30's 'inevitable'. Recommended fix (option A): reach feeds the SAME accumulator at a slower rate, so the Metropole is the longest-lived shape and still breaks - usually via the Slow Fade (E6). CONFIRMED by Ben 2026-08-20 (NR-356 resolved, option A): 'logistics should be capable of determining reach... reach feeds strain' - the inflow reads the same logistics/reach substrate as everything else, per BL-325 ruling 3 (one reach field).
items.design: One additional inflow term on BL-504's accumulator scaled by reach-derived exposure (routes/dependencies held abroad). HISTORY.md Stage 5 (hegemony fails its final audition) later becomes a parameterisation of this, not a second system. RULED 2026-08-20 (Ben, NR-356 resolved, option A): reach feeds strain, and the inflow reads the same logistics/reach substrate as everything else per BL-325 ruling 3 (one reach field) - no longer pending; the filed shape stands as ruled.

items.title: Render the province, not the hex: province-grain canvas with softened borders
items.design:
## Ben's framing (2026-08-20)

Decouple play from tiles: rather than rendering hexes, render the PROVINCE as a
unit, with graphics that blend neighbouring tiles into each other, softening the
borders.

Filed as the presentation half of that session's idea. The MECHANICAL half — a
derived per-province building limit, so productivity packs into a smaller space —
is separable, does not depend on this, and was taken first (Ben's call, same
session: "B for the limit, and file rendering into backlog").

## Why this is design-owed and not ready to build

It is a THIRD position on a grain question that already has two dated rulings, and
only Ben can move it:

1. **2026-08-13, BL-315 ruling 2** — units are tokens on the TILE map, explicitly
   "not armies at province grain".
2. **2026-08-19, BL-467** — reconciled by SPLITTING the grains: command stays the
   tile, the province supplies the ENGAGEMENT envelope. Both rulings are Ben's,
   five days apart, and compatible.

Rendering the province as the play unit is neither of those. It moves the grain the
player SEES and CLICKS, which is the grain the tile-token ruling was about. Landing
this without a ruling would overturn 2026-08-13 silently.

## What it reaches

Wider than it first reads, because the tile is the current key everywhere:

- `body_surface_canvas.cpp` — the hex raster itself, plus the blend between
  neighbouring compositions. The softening is the actual graphics work and has no
  precedent in the codebase: every current surface draws crisp hexes.
- **Every lens.** All eleven overlay modes key on tile fields (LENSES.md). A
  province-grain canvas needs a per-province reduction of each — a mean, a
  dominant class, or a deliberate refusal — decided lens by lens.
- **Selection.** SELECTION.md's single-click-selects / double-click-navigates model
  is tile-addressed; a province becomes a new selectable entity kind with its own
  polymorphic content builder.
- `icons.cpp` — building markers currently sit at tile centres.
- The **Generation Ledger** (GENERATION_LEDGER.md) explains a TILE's derivation.
  Its per-tile breadcrumb is the strongest argument for keeping tiles visible
  somewhere, even if the play grain moves.

## Open questions for the design session

- Does the tile survive as an inspection grain (zoom-in, or the ledger only), or
  does it become internal entirely?
- What does a province's terrain READ as, when its tiles differ? A dominant
  composition loses the mixture that TILES.md's two-axis model exists to express.
- Do buildings still sit at tile positions inside the rendered province, or float
  at province grain? BL-467 keeps units tile-canonical; buildings diverging from
  that would be a second grain split.
- What happens to the 2x2 block structure the partition already uses (BL-466 ids
  are body_rank | block_raster_index | component)? Provinces average ~4 tiles on
  the reference world (32,044 land tiles to 8,294 provinces), so a rendered
  province is SMALL — is that the unit Ben pictures, or does this item also want a
  coarser partition?

## Dependency

BL-466 (province partition) is landed, so the data exists. Nothing else blocks the
design; the grain ruling blocks the build.
